57/// @brief Per-type tolerance used by approximate floating-point comparisons.
58/// @details Returned by @c Tolerance<T>::value() and consumed by @c isApproxZero.
59/// Specialized for @c float, @c double, and @c long double. Instantiating on
60/// any other @c T is an "incomplete type" compile error by design — callers
61/// must opt in by adding a specialization.
62template<typename T>
63struct Tolerance;
64template<>
65struct Tolerance<float>
66{
67 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr float value() noexcept { return 1e-8f; }
68};
69template<>
70struct Tolerance<double>
71{
72 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr double value() noexcept { return 1e-15; }
73};
74template<>
75struct Tolerance<long double>
76{
77 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr long double value() noexcept { return 1e-18L; }
78};
79//@}
80

85/// @c double, and @c long double; instantiating on any other @c T is a
86/// compile error by design.
87template<typename T>
88struct Delta;
89template<>
90struct Delta<float>
91{
92 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr float value() noexcept { return 1e-5f; }
93};
94template<>
95struct Delta<double>

97 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr double value() noexcept { return 1e-9; }
98};

100struct Delta<long double>

102 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr long double value() noexcept { return 1e-12L; }
103};

107/// @brief Per-type largest representable value (mirrors @c std::numeric_limits::max).
108/// @details Returned by @c Maximum<T>::value(). The host fallback (`#else`
109/// branch) forwards to @c std::numeric_limits so any @c T with a
110/// specialization there works; the CUDA-device branch uses
111/// @c ::cuda::std::numeric_limits; the HIP branch hard-codes a handful of
112/// common types because @c std::numeric_limits is unavailable on the device
113/// in some HIP toolchains.
114template<typename T>
115struct Maximum;
116#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
117template<typename T>
118struct Maximum
119{
120 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr T value() noexcept { return ::cuda::std::numeric_limits<T>::max(); }
121};
122#elif defined(__HIP__)
123template<>
124struct Maximum<int>
125{
126 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr int value() noexcept { return 2147483647; }
127};
128template<>
129struct Maximum<uint32_t>
130{
131 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr uint32_t value() noexcept { return 4294967295u; }
132};
133template<>
134struct Maximum<float>
135{
136 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr float value() noexcept { return 1e+38f; }
137};
138template<>
139struct Maximum<double>
140{
141 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr double value() noexcept { return 1e+308; }
142};
143#else
144template<typename T>
145struct Maximum
146{
147 [[nodiscard]] static constexpr T value() noexcept { return std::numeric_limits<T>::max(); }
148};
149#endif

152/// @brief Return @c true if @c |x| is below @c Tolerance<Type>::value().
153template<typename Type>
154__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr bool isApproxZero(const Type& x) noexcept
155{
156 return !(x > Tolerance<Type>::value()) && !(x < -Tolerance<Type>::value());
157}
158
159/// @brief Same-type minimum (the primary template).
160template<typename Type>
161__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Type Min(Type a, Type b) noexcept
162{
163 return (a < b) ? a : b;
164}
165// Mixed integer-type tiebreakers: the templated `Min<Type>` requires both
166// args to deduce to the same `Type`, so calls like `Min(uint32_t, size_t)`
167// would otherwise fall through to the float/double overloads with equal
168// implicit-conversion cost — ambiguous. These integer overloads win.
169__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int32_t Min(int32_t a, int32_t b) noexcept
170{
171 return a < b ? a : b;
172}
173__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr uint32_t Min(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) noexcept
174{
175 return a < b ? a : b;
176}
177__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline float Min(float a, float b) noexcept
178{
179 return fminf(a, b);
180}
181__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline double Min(double a, double b) noexcept
182{
183 return fmin(a, b);
184}
185/// @brief Same-type maximum (the primary template).
186template<typename Type>
187__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Type Max(Type a, Type b) noexcept
188{
189 return (a > b) ? a : b;
190}
191// See Min above: these integer overloads disambiguate mixed-int calls.
192__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int32_t Max(int32_t a, int32_t b) noexcept
193{
194 return a > b ? a : b;
195}
196__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr uint32_t Max(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) noexcept
197{
198 return a > b ? a : b;
199}
200__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline float Max(float a, float b) noexcept
201{
202 return fmaxf(a, b);
203}
204__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline double Max(double a, double b) noexcept
205{
206 return fmax(a, b);
207}
208//@{
209/// @brief Clamp @c x to the closed interval [@c a, @c b].
210__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline float Clamp(float x, float a, float b) noexcept
211{
212 return Max(Min(x, b), a);
213}
214__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline double Clamp(double x, double a, double b) noexcept
215{
216 return Max(Min(x, b), a);
217}
218//@}

302//@{
303/// @brief Round @c x to the nearest 32-bit signed integer, with halfway cases
304/// rounded toward +inf.
305/// @details Exact for every input, because @c x - floor(x) has no rounding
306/// error. The shorter @c floor(x + 0.5) rounds the sum first, which moves
307/// e.g. @c 0.49999997f to 1 and @c 8388609.f to 8388610.
308__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline int32_t Round(float x) noexcept
309{
310 const float f = floorf(x);
311 return int32_t(f) + (x - f >= 0.5f);
312}
313__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline int32_t Round(double x) noexcept
314{
315 const double f = floor(x);
316 return int32_t(f) + (x - f >= 0.5);
317}
318//@}
319
320/// @brief Round each component of @c xyz to its closest integer coordinate.
321/// @details Forward declaration of the primary template — there is no
322/// definition here. Callers resolve to one of the @c float / @c double
323/// overloads below. Both use the scalar @c Round rule (nearest, halfway cases
324/// toward +inf), so float and double inputs with the same value yield the
325/// same integer coordinate.
326template<typename CoordT, typename RealT, template<typename> class Vec3T>
327__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline CoordT Round(const Vec3T<RealT>& xyz) noexcept;
328
329/// @brief Round each component to its closest integer, halfway cases toward +inf.
330template<typename CoordT, template<typename> class Vec3T>
331__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline CoordT Round(const Vec3T<float>& xyz) noexcept
332{
333 return CoordT(Round(xyz[0]), Round(xyz[1]), Round(xyz[2]));
334}
335
336/// @brief Double-precision variant of @c Round — see the @c float overload above.
337template<typename CoordT, template<typename> class Vec3T>
338__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline CoordT Round(const Vec3T<double>& xyz) noexcept
339{
340 return CoordT(Round(xyz[0]), Round(xyz[1]), Round(xyz[2]));
341}
342
343/// @brief Round each component of @c xyz down (toward -inf) into a @c CoordT.
344template<typename CoordT, typename RealT, template<typename> class Vec3T>
345__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline CoordT RoundDown(const Vec3T<RealT>& xyz) noexcept
346{
347 return CoordT(Floor(xyz[0]), Floor(xyz[1]), Floor(xyz[2]));
348}

362/// Return the sign of the given value as an integer (either -1, 0 or 1).
363template<typename T>
364__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr T Sign(const T& x) noexcept
365{
366 return ((T(0) < x) ? T(1) : T(0)) - ((x < T(0)) ? T(1) : T(0));
367}

369/// @brief Return the component index (0, 1, or 2) of the smallest element of @c v.
370/// @note Ties resolve to the lowest index (i.e. x beats y, y beats z).
371template<typename Vec3T>
372__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int MinIndex(const Vec3T& v) noexcept
373{
374#if 0
375 static const int hashTable[8] = {2, 1, 9, 1, 2, 9, 0, 0}; //9 are dummy values
376 const int hashKey = ((v[0] < v[1]) << 2) + ((v[0] < v[2]) << 1) + (v[1] < v[2]); // ?*4+?*2+?*1
377 return hashTable[hashKey];
378#else
379 if (v[0] < v[1] && v[0] < v[2])
380 return 0;
381 if (v[1] < v[2])
382 return 1;
383 else
384 return 2;
385#endif
386}

389/// @note Ties resolve to the lowest index (i.e. x beats y, y beats z).
390template<typename Vec3T>
391__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr int MaxIndex(const Vec3T& v) noexcept

395 const int hashKey = ((v[0] > v[1]) << 2) + ((v[0] > v[2]) << 1) + (v[1] > v[2]); // ?*4+?*2+?*1
396 return hashTable[hashKey];
397#else

399 return 0;
400 if (v[1] > v[2])
401 return 1;
402 else
403 return 2;

405}

407/// @brief round up byteSize to the nearest wordSize, e.g. to align to machine word: AlignUp<sizeof(size_t)(n)
408///
409/// @details both wordSize and byteSize are in byte units
410template<uint64_t wordSize>
411__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr uint64_t AlignUp(uint64_t byteCount) noexcept
412{
413 const uint64_t r = byteCount % wordSize;
414 return r ? byteCount - r + wordSize : byteCount;
415}

423/// @brief Signed (i, j, k) 32-bit integer coordinate class, similar to openvdb::math::Coord
424class Coord
425{
426 int32_t mVec[3]; // private member data - three signed index coordinates
427public:
428 using ValueType = int32_t;
429 using IndexType = uint32_t;
430
431 /// @brief Initialize all coordinates to zero.
432 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord() noexcept
433 : mVec{0, 0, 0}
434 {
435 }
436
437 /// @brief Initializes all coordinates to the given signed integer.
438 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Coord(ValueType n) noexcept
439 : mVec{n, n, n}
440 {
441 }
442
443 /// @brief Initializes coordinate to the given signed integers.
444 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord(ValueType i, ValueType j, ValueType k) noexcept
445 : mVec{i, j, k}
446 {
447 }
448
449 /// @brief Read three signed integers from @a ptr (no bounds check).
450 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord(ValueType* ptr) noexcept
451 : mVec{ptr[0], ptr[1], ptr[2]}
452 {
453 }
454
455 //@{
456 /// @brief Named component accessors (x = mVec[0], y = mVec[1], z = mVec[2]).
457 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t x() const noexcept { return mVec[0]; }
458 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t y() const noexcept { return mVec[1]; }
459 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t z() const noexcept { return mVec[2]; }
460
461 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t& x() noexcept { return mVec[0]; }
462 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t& y() noexcept { return mVec[1]; }
463 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t& z() noexcept { return mVec[2]; }
464 //@}
465
466 /// @brief Largest representable @c Coord (all components = INT32_MAX).
467 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr Coord max() noexcept { return Coord(int32_t((1u << 31) - 1)); }
468
469 /// @brief Smallest representable @c Coord (all components = INT32_MIN).
470 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr Coord min() noexcept { return Coord(-int32_t((1u << 31) - 1) - 1); }
471
472 /// @brief Byte size of a @c Coord (always 12 on a 32-bit @c int32_t platform).
473 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr size_t memUsage() noexcept { return sizeof(Coord); }
474
475 /// @brief Return a const reference to the given Coord component.
476 /// @warning The argument is assumed to be 0, 1, or 2.
477 __hostdev__ constexpr const ValueType& operator[](IndexType i) const noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i < 3); return mVec[i]; }
478
479 /// @brief Return a non-const reference to the given Coord component.
480 /// @warning The argument is assumed to be 0, 1, or 2.
481 __hostdev__ constexpr ValueType& operator[](IndexType i) noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i < 3); return mVec[i]; }
482
483 /// @brief Assignment operator that works with openvdb::Coord
484 template<typename CoordT>
485 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& operator=(const CoordT& other) noexcept
486 {
487 static_assert(sizeof(Coord) == sizeof(CoordT), "Mis-matched sizeof");
488 mVec[0] = other[0];
489 mVec[1] = other[1];
490 mVec[2] = other[2];
491 return *this;
492 }
493
494 /// @brief Return a new instance with coordinates masked by the given unsigned integer.
495 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord operator&(IndexType n) const noexcept { return Coord(mVec[0] & n, mVec[1] & n, mVec[2] & n); }
496
497 /// @brief Return a new instance with coordinates left-shifted by the given unsigned integer.
498 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord operator<<(IndexType n) const noexcept { return Coord(mVec[0] << n, mVec[1] << n, mVec[2] << n); }
499
500 /// @brief Return a new instance with coordinates right-shifted by the given unsigned integer.
501 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord operator>>(IndexType n) const noexcept { return Coord(mVec[0] >> n, mVec[1] >> n, mVec[2] >> n); }
502
503 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically less than the given Coord.
504 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator<(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept
505 {
506 return mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? true
507 : mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? false
508 : mVec[1] < rhs[1] ? true
509 : mVec[1] > rhs[1] ? false
510 : mVec[2] < rhs[2] ? true : false;
511 }
512
513 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically less or equal to the given Coord.
514 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator<=(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept
515 {
516 return mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? true
517 : mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? false
518 : mVec[1] < rhs[1] ? true
519 : mVec[1] > rhs[1] ? false
520 : mVec[2] <=rhs[2] ? true : false;
521 }
522
523 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically greater than the given Coord.
524 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator>(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept
525 {
526 return mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? true
527 : mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? false
528 : mVec[1] > rhs[1] ? true
529 : mVec[1] < rhs[1] ? false
530 : mVec[2] > rhs[2] ? true : false;
531 }
532
533 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically greater or equal to the given Coord.
534 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator>=(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept
535 {
536 return mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? true
537 : mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? false
538 : mVec[1] > rhs[1] ? true
539 : mVec[1] < rhs[1] ? false
540 : mVec[2] >=rhs[2] ? true : false;
541 }
542
543 /// @brief Return true iff every component matches @a rhs.
544 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept { return mVec[0] == rhs[0] && mVec[1] == rhs[1] && mVec[2] == rhs[2]; }
545 /// @brief Return true iff any component differs from @a rhs.
546 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept { return mVec[0] != rhs[0] || mVec[1] != rhs[1] || mVec[2] != rhs[2]; }
547 /// @brief In-place component-wise bitwise AND with the given mask.
548 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& operator&=(int n) noexcept
549 {
550 mVec[0] &= n;
551 mVec[1] &= n;
552 mVec[2] &= n;
553 return *this;
554 }
555 /// @brief In-place left-shift of every component by @a n bits.
556 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& operator<<=(uint32_t n) noexcept
557 {
558 mVec[0] <<= n;
559 mVec[1] <<= n;
560 mVec[2] <<= n;
561 return *this;
562 }
563 /// @brief In-place right-shift of every component by @a n bits.
564 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& operator>>=(uint32_t n) noexcept
565 {
566 mVec[0] >>= n;
567 mVec[1] >>= n;
568 mVec[2] >>= n;
569 return *this;
570 }
571 /// @brief Add a scalar to every component in place.
572 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& operator+=(int n) noexcept
573 {
574 mVec[0] += n;
575 mVec[1] += n;
576 mVec[2] += n;
577 return *this;
578 }
579 /// @brief Component-wise sum of two coordinates.
580 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord operator+(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept { return Coord(mVec[0] + rhs[0], mVec[1] + rhs[1], mVec[2] + rhs[2]); }
581 /// @brief Component-wise difference of two coordinates.
582 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord operator-(const Coord& rhs) const noexcept { return Coord(mVec[0] - rhs[0], mVec[1] - rhs[1], mVec[2] - rhs[2]); }
583 /// @brief Component-wise negation.
584 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord operator-() const noexcept { return Coord(-mVec[0], -mVec[1], -mVec[2]); }
585 /// @brief In-place component-wise addition with another coordinate.
586 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& operator+=(const Coord& rhs) noexcept
587 {
588 mVec[0] += rhs[0];
589 mVec[1] += rhs[1];
590 mVec[2] += rhs[2];
591 return *this;
592 }
593 /// @brief In-place component-wise subtraction with another coordinate.
594 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& operator-=(const Coord& rhs) noexcept
595 {
596 mVec[0] -= rhs[0];
597 mVec[1] -= rhs[1];
598 mVec[2] -= rhs[2];
599 return *this;
600 }
601
602 /// @brief Perform a component-wise minimum with the other Coord.
603 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& minComponent(const Coord& other) noexcept
604 {
605 if (other[0] < mVec[0])
606 mVec[0] = other[0];
607 if (other[1] < mVec[1])
608 mVec[1] = other[1];
609 if (other[2] < mVec[2])
610 mVec[2] = other[2];
611 return *this;
612 }
613
614 /// @brief Perform a component-wise maximum with the other Coord.
615 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord& maxComponent(const Coord& other) noexcept
616 {
617 if (other[0] > mVec[0])
618 mVec[0] = other[0];
619 if (other[1] > mVec[1])
620 mVec[1] = other[1];
621 if (other[2] > mVec[2])
622 mVec[2] = other[2];
623 return *this;
624 }
625#if defined(__CUDACC__) // the following functions only run on the GPU!
626 /// @brief Device-only @c atomicMin component-wise.
627 __device__ inline Coord& minComponentAtomic(const Coord& other) noexcept
628 {
629 atomicMin(&mVec[0], other[0]);
630 atomicMin(&mVec[1], other[1]);
631 atomicMin(&mVec[2], other[2]);
632 return *this;
633 }
634 /// @brief Device-only @c atomicMax component-wise.
635 __device__ inline Coord& maxComponentAtomic(const Coord& other) noexcept
636 {
637 atomicMax(&mVec[0], other[0]);
638 atomicMax(&mVec[1], other[1]);
639 atomicMax(&mVec[2], other[2]);
640 return *this;
641 }
642#endif
643
644 /// @brief Return a new @c Coord offset component-by-component by @a (dx, dy, dz).
645 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord offsetBy(ValueType dx, ValueType dy, ValueType dz) const noexcept
646 {
647 return Coord(mVec[0] + dx, mVec[1] + dy, mVec[2] + dz);
648 }
649
650 /// @brief Return a new @c Coord offset by the same scalar @a n in every component.
651 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord offsetBy(ValueType n) const noexcept { return this->offsetBy(n, n, n); }
652
653 /// Return true if any of the components of @a a are smaller than the
654 /// corresponding components of @a b.
655 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static inline constexpr bool lessThan(const Coord& a, const Coord& b) noexcept
656 {
657 return (a[0] < b[0] || a[1] < b[1] || a[2] < b[2]);
658 }
659
660 /// @brief Return the largest integer coordinates that are not greater
661 /// than @a xyz (node centered conversion).
662 template<typename Vec3T>
663 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static Coord Floor(const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept { return Coord(math::Floor(xyz[0]), math::Floor(xyz[1]), math::Floor(xyz[2])); }
664
665 /// @brief Return a hash key derived from the existing coordinates.
666 /// @details The hash function is originally taken from the SIGGRAPH paper:
667 /// "VDB: High-resolution sparse volumes with dynamic topology"
668 /// and the prime numbers are modified based on the ACM Transactions on Graphics paper:
669 /// "Real-time 3D reconstruction at scale using voxel hashing" (the second number had a typo!)
670 template<int Log2N = 3 + 4 + 5>
671 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr uint32_t hash() const noexcept { return ((1 << Log2N) - 1) & (mVec[0] * 73856093 ^ mVec[1] * 19349669 ^ mVec[2] * 83492791); }
672
673 /// @brief Return the octant of this Coord
674 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr uint8_t octant() const noexcept { return uint8_t((uint8_t(bool(mVec[0] & (1u << 31)))) |
675 (uint8_t(bool(mVec[1] & (1u << 31))) << 1) |
676 (uint8_t(bool(mVec[2] & (1u << 31))) << 2)); }
677
678 /// @brief Return a single precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
679 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3<float> asVec3s() const noexcept;
680
681 /// @brief Return a double precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
682 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3<double> asVec3d() const noexcept;
683
684 /// @brief Identity (Coord is already integer); provided so generic code
685 /// can call @c .round() uniformly on @c Coord and @c Vec3<T>.
686 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Coord round() const noexcept { return *this; }
687}; // Coord class
688

690/// @brief Type alias for Coord so we have a consistent naming convention
691using Coord3 = Coord;
692
693
694template <typename T>
695class Vec2;
696
697/// @brief Signed (i, j) 32-bit integer coordinate class, similar to openvdb::math::Coord
698class Coord2
699{
700 int32_t mVec[2]; // private member data - three signed index coordinates
701public:
702 using ValueType = int32_t;
703 using IndexType = uint32_t;
704
705 /// @brief Initialize all coordinates to zero.
706 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2() noexcept
707 : mVec{0, 0}
708 {
709 }
710
711 /// @brief Initializes all coordinates to the given signed integer.
712 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Coord2(ValueType n) noexcept
713 : mVec{n, n}
714 {
715 }
716
717 /// @brief Initializes coordinate to the given signed integers.
718 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2(ValueType i, ValueType j) noexcept
719 : mVec{i, j}
720 {
721 }
722
723 /// @brief Read two signed integers from @a ptr (no bounds check).
724 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2(ValueType* ptr) noexcept
725 : mVec{ptr[0], ptr[1]}
726 {
727 }
728
729 //@{
730 /// @brief Named component accessors (x = mVec[0], y = mVec[1]).
731 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t x() const noexcept { return mVec[0]; }
732 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t y() const noexcept { return mVec[1]; }
733
734 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t& x() noexcept { return mVec[0]; }
735 __hostdev__ constexpr int32_t& y() noexcept { return mVec[1]; }
736 //@}
737
738 /// @brief Largest representable @c Coord2 (all components = INT32_MAX).
739 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr Coord2 max() noexcept { return Coord2(int32_t((1u << 31) - 1)); }
740
741 /// @brief Smallest representable @c Coord2 (all components = INT32_MIN).
742 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr Coord2 min() noexcept { return Coord2(-int32_t((1u << 31) - 1) - 1); }
743
744 /// @brief Byte size of a @c Coord2 (always 8 on a 32-bit @c int32_t platform).
745 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr size_t memUsage() noexcept { return sizeof(Coord2); }
746
747 /// @brief Return a const reference to the given Coord component.
748 /// @warning The argument is assumed to be 0 or 1,
749 __hostdev__ constexpr const ValueType& operator[](IndexType i) const noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i < 2); return mVec[i]; }
750
751 /// @brief Return a non-const reference to the given Coord component.
752 /// @warning The argument is assumed to be 0 or 1.
753 __hostdev__ constexpr ValueType& operator[](IndexType i) noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i < 2); return mVec[i]; }
754
755 /// @brief Assignment operator that works with openvdb::Coord
756 template<typename CoordT>
757 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& operator=(const CoordT& other) noexcept
758 {
759 static_assert(sizeof(Coord2) == sizeof(CoordT), "Mis-matched sizeof");
760 mVec[0] = other[0];
761 mVec[1] = other[1];
762 return *this;
763 }
764
765 /// @brief Return a new instance with coordinates masked by the given unsigned integer.
766 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 operator&(IndexType n) const noexcept { return Coord2(mVec[0] & n, mVec[1] & n); }
767
768 /// @brief Return a new instance with coordinates left-shifted by the given unsigned integer.
769 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 operator<<(IndexType n) const noexcept { return Coord2(mVec[0] << n, mVec[1] << n); }
770
771 /// @brief Return a new instance with coordinates right-shifted by the given unsigned integer.
772 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 operator>>(IndexType n) const noexcept { return Coord2(mVec[0] >> n, mVec[1] >> n); }
773
774 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically less than the given Coord.
775 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator<(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept
776 {
777 return mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? true
778 : mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? false
779 : mVec[1] < rhs[1] ? true : false;
780 }
781
782 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically less or equal to the given Coord.
783 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator<=(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept
784 {
785 return mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? true
786 : mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? false
787 : mVec[1] <= rhs[1] ? true : false;
788 }
789
790 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically greater than the given Coord.
791 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator>(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept
792 {
793 return mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? true
794 : mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? false
795 : mVec[1] > rhs[1] ? true : false;
796 }
797
798 /// @brief Return true if this Coord is lexicographically greater or equal to the given Coord.
799 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator>=(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept
800 {
801 return mVec[0] > rhs[0] ? true
802 : mVec[0] < rhs[0] ? false
803 : mVec[1] >= rhs[1] ? true : false;
804 }
805
806 /// @brief Return true iff every component matches @a rhs.
807 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept { return mVec[0] == rhs[0] && mVec[1] == rhs[1]; }
808 /// @brief Return true iff any component differs from @a rhs.
809 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept { return mVec[0] != rhs[0] || mVec[1] != rhs[1]; }
810 /// @brief In-place component-wise bitwise AND with the given mask.
811 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& operator&=(int n) noexcept
812 {
813 mVec[0] &= n;
814 mVec[1] &= n;
815 return *this;
816 }
817 /// @brief In-place left-shift of every component by @a n bits.
818 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& operator<<=(uint32_t n) noexcept
819 {
820 mVec[0] <<= n;
821 mVec[1] <<= n;
822 return *this;
823 }
824 /// @brief In-place right-shift of every component by @a n bits.
825 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& operator>>=(uint32_t n) noexcept
826 {
827 mVec[0] >>= n;
828 mVec[1] >>= n;
829 return *this;
830 }
831 /// @brief Add a scalar to every component in place.
832 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& operator+=(int n) noexcept
833 {
834 mVec[0] += n;
835 mVec[1] += n;
836 return *this;
837 }
838 /// @brief Component-wise sum of two coordinates.
839 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 operator+(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept { return Coord2(mVec[0] + rhs[0], mVec[1] + rhs[1]); }
840 /// @brief Component-wise difference of two coordinates.
841 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 operator-(const Coord2& rhs) const noexcept { return Coord2(mVec[0] - rhs[0], mVec[1] - rhs[1]); }
842 /// @brief Component-wise negation.
843 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 operator-() const noexcept { return Coord2(-mVec[0], -mVec[1]); }
844 /// @brief In-place component-wise addition with another coordinate.
845 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& operator+=(const Coord2& rhs) noexcept
846 {
847 mVec[0] += rhs[0];
848 mVec[1] += rhs[1];
849 return *this;
850 }
851 /// @brief In-place component-wise subtraction with another coordinate.
852 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& operator-=(const Coord2& rhs) noexcept
853 {
854 mVec[0] -= rhs[0];
855 mVec[1] -= rhs[1];
856 return *this;
857 }
858
859 /// @brief Perform a component-wise minimum with the other Coord.
860 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& minComponent(const Coord2& other) noexcept
861 {
862 if (other[0] < mVec[0])
863 mVec[0] = other[0];
864 if (other[1] < mVec[1])
865 mVec[1] = other[1];
866 return *this;
867 }
868
869 /// @brief Perform a component-wise maximum with the other Coord.
870 __hostdev__ constexpr Coord2& maxComponent(const Coord2& other) noexcept
871 {
872 if (other[0] > mVec[0])
873 mVec[0] = other[0];
874 if (other[1] > mVec[1])
875 mVec[1] = other[1];
876 return *this;
877 }
878#if defined(__CUDACC__) // the following functions only run on the GPU!
879 /// @brief Device-only @c atomicMin component-wise.
880 __device__ inline Coord2& minComponentAtomic(const Coord2& other) noexcept
881 {
882 atomicMin(&mVec[0], other[0]);
883 atomicMin(&mVec[1], other[1]);
884 return *this;
885 }
886 /// @brief Device-only @c atomicMax component-wise.
887 __device__ inline Coord2& maxComponentAtomic(const Coord2& other) noexcept
888 {
889 atomicMax(&mVec[0], other[0]);
890 atomicMax(&mVec[1], other[1]);
891 return *this;
892 }
893#endif
894
895 /// @brief Return a new @c Coord2 offset component-by-component by @a (dx, dy).
896 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 offsetBy(ValueType dx, ValueType dy) const noexcept
897 {
898 return Coord2(mVec[0] + dx, mVec[1] + dy);
899 }
900
901 /// @brief Return a new @c Coord2 offset by the same scalar @a n in both components.
902 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 offsetBy(ValueType n) const noexcept { return this->offsetBy(n, n); }
903
904 /// Return true if any of the components of @a a are smaller than the
905 /// corresponding components of @a b.
906 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static inline constexpr bool lessThan(const Coord2& a, const Coord2& b) noexcept
907 {
908 return (a[0] < b[0] || a[1] < b[1]);
909 }
910
911 /// @brief Return the largest integer coordinates that are not greater
912 /// than @a xyz (node centered conversion).
913 template<typename Vec2T>
914 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static Coord2 Floor(const Vec2T& xy) noexcept { return Coord2(math::Floor(xy[0]), math::Floor(xy[1])); }
915
916 /// @brief Return a single precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
917 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec2<float> asVec2s() const noexcept;
918
919 /// @brief Return a double precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
920 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec2<double> asVec2d() const noexcept;
921
922 /// @brief Identity (Coord2 is already integer); provided so generic code
923 /// can call @c .round() uniformly on @c Coord2 and @c Vec2<T>.
924 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Coord2 round() const noexcept { return *this; }
925}; // Coord2 class
926
927// ----------------------------> VecBase <-----------------------------------
928
929/// @brief Base class for fixed-size vectors. Provides shared element-wise
930/// arithmetic, scalar arithmetic, equality, length/dot reductions,
931/// component min/max, and integer-coord rounding. Derived classes provide
932/// constructors and any dimension-specific extras (e.g. cross/outer on Vec3).
933template<typename T, int N>
934class VecBase
935{
936protected:
937 T mVec[N];
938
939public:
940 using ValueType = T;
941 static constexpr int SIZE = N;
942
943 /// @brief Default-construct (mVec is left uninitialized for trivially-default-constructible @c T).
944 VecBase() noexcept = default;
945
946protected:
947 /// @brief Variadic component-init ctor — used only by derived ctors
948 /// (`Vec2(T x, T y) : Base(x, y) {}`). The member-init list directly
949 /// initializes @c mVec, avoiding the default-construct-then-assign that
950 /// a body-assignment ctor would impose on a non-fundamental @c T.
951 template<typename... Args>
952 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr VecBase(Args... args) noexcept : mVec{T(args)...}
953 {
954 static_assert(sizeof...(Args) == N, "VecBase: wrong number of constructor arguments");
955 }
956
957 /// @brief Return a @c Derived whose component @c i is @c f(i), built through its
958 /// N-component constructor. This is constexpr-valid in C++17 without first
959 /// value-initializing a result and overwriting it.
960 template<typename Derived, typename F, int... I>
961 __hostdev__ static constexpr Derived generate(F f, std::integer_sequence<int, I...>) noexcept
962 {
963 return Derived(typename Derived::ValueType(f(I))...);
964 }
965 template<typename Derived, typename F>
966 __hostdev__ static constexpr Derived generate(F f) noexcept
967 {
968 return generate<Derived>(f, std::make_integer_sequence<int, N>{});
969 }
970
971public:
972 /// @brief Indexed element access. Asserts 0 <= i < N in debug builds.
973 __hostdev__ constexpr const T& operator[](int i) const noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i >= 0 && i < N); return mVec[i]; }
974 __hostdev__ constexpr T& operator[](int i) noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i >= 0 && i < N); return mVec[i]; }
975
976 __hostdev__ constexpr const T& x() const noexcept { return mVec[0]; }
977 __hostdev__ constexpr T& x() noexcept { return mVec[0]; }
978 __hostdev__ constexpr const T& y() const noexcept { static_assert(N >= 2, "VecBase::y() requires N >= 2"); return mVec[1]; }
979 __hostdev__ constexpr T& y() noexcept { static_assert(N >= 2, "VecBase::y() requires N >= 2"); return mVec[1]; }
980 __hostdev__ constexpr const T& z() const noexcept { static_assert(N >= 3, "VecBase::z() requires N >= 3"); return mVec[2]; }
981 __hostdev__ constexpr T& z() noexcept { static_assert(N >= 3, "VecBase::z() requires N >= 3"); return mVec[2]; }
982 __hostdev__ constexpr const T& w() const noexcept { static_assert(N >= 4, "VecBase::w() requires N >= 4"); return mVec[3]; }
983 __hostdev__ constexpr T& w() noexcept { static_assert(N >= 4, "VecBase::w() requires N >= 4"); return mVec[3]; }
984
985 /// @brief raw pointer to the underlying N-element storage
986 __hostdev__ constexpr T* asPointer() noexcept { return mVec; }
987 __hostdev__ constexpr const T* asPointer() const noexcept { return mVec; }
988
989 // ---- generic element-wise helpers (taking/returning Derived) ----
990
991 /// @brief Return @c *this + @a rhs as a @c Derived.
992 template<typename Derived>
993 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived plus(const Derived& rhs) const noexcept {
994 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mVec[i] + rhs[i]; });
995 }
996 /// @brief Return @c *this - @a rhs as a @c Derived.
997 template<typename Derived>
998 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived minus(const Derived& rhs) const noexcept {
999 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mVec[i] - rhs[i]; });
1000 }
1001 /// @brief Return component-wise @c *this * @a rhs as a @c Derived (Hadamard product).
1002 template<typename Derived>
1003 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived mul(const Derived& rhs) const noexcept {
1004 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mVec[i] * rhs[i]; });
1005 }
1006 /// @brief Return component-wise @c *this / @a rhs as a @c Derived.
1007 template<typename Derived>
1008 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived div(const Derived& rhs) const noexcept {
1009 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mVec[i] / rhs[i]; });
1010 }
1011 /// @brief Return @c -(*this) as a @c Derived.
1012 template<typename Derived>
1013 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived negate() const noexcept {
1014 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return -mVec[i]; });
1015 }
1016 /// @brief Return @c s * (*this) as a @c Derived (scalar broadcast).
1017 template<typename Derived>
1018 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived scale(T s) const noexcept {
1019 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mVec[i] * s; });
1020 }
1021 /// @brief Return @c (*this) / @a s element-wise as a @c Derived. Floating-point
1022 /// @c T multiplies by the reciprocal @c 1/s; integer @c T divides each element,
1023 /// since @c 1/s would truncate to zero.
1024 template<typename Derived>
1025 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived divideBy(T s) const noexcept {
1026 if constexpr (std::is_floating_point<T>::value) {
1027 return this->template scale<Derived>(T(1) / s);
1028 } else {
1029 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mVec[i] / s; });
1030 }
1031 }
1032 /// @brief Return a unit-length copy (@c *this divided by @c length()) as a @c Derived.
1033 /// Const, non-mutating counterpart of the derived @c normalize(). Not @c constexpr —
1034 /// @c length() calls @c Sqrt.
1035 template<typename Derived>
1036 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] Derived normalized() const noexcept {
1037 return this->template divideBy<Derived>(this->length());
1038 }
1039
1040 // ---- in-place compound assignment helpers ----
1041
1042 /// @brief Component-wise add @a rhs into @c *this and return @c *this.
1043 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& addAssign(const VecBase& rhs) noexcept {
1044 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) mVec[i] += rhs.mVec[i];
1045 return *this;
1046 }
1047 /// @brief Component-wise subtract @a rhs from @c *this and return @c *this.
1048 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& subAssign(const VecBase& rhs) noexcept {
1049 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) mVec[i] -= rhs.mVec[i];
1050 return *this;
1051 }
1052 /// @brief Component-wise multiply @c *this by @a rhs (Hadamard product) and return @c *this.
1053 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& mulAssign(const VecBase& rhs) noexcept {
1054 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) mVec[i] *= rhs.mVec[i];
1055 return *this;
1056 }
1057 /// @brief Component-wise divide @c *this by @a rhs and return @c *this.
1058 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& divAssign(const VecBase& rhs) noexcept {
1059 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) mVec[i] /= rhs.mVec[i];
1060 return *this;
1061 }
1062 /// @brief Multiply every component by scalar @a s in place; return @c *this.
1063 /// @a s is taken by value so @c v *= v[0] scales every component by the original value.
1064 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& scaleAssign(T s) noexcept {
1065 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) mVec[i] *= s;
1066 return *this;
1067 }
1068 /// @brief Divide every component by scalar @a s in place; return @c *this.
1069 /// Uses the same floating-point reciprocal / integer per-element split as
1070 /// @c divideBy. @a s is taken by value so @c v /= v[0] is safe.
1071 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& divideAssignScalar(T s) noexcept {
1072 if constexpr (std::is_floating_point<T>::value) {
1073 return this->scaleAssign(T(1) / s);
1074 } else {
1075 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) mVec[i] /= s;
1076 return *this;
1077 }
1078 }
1079
1080 /// @brief Return @c true iff every component compares equal to @a rhs.
1081 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool equals(const VecBase& rhs) const noexcept {
1082 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) if (mVec[i] != rhs.mVec[i]) return false;
1083 return true;
1084 }
1085
1086 // ---- reductions ----
1087
1088 /// @brief dot product. @a V must have @c operator[] valid for 0..N-1.
1089 /// Sums in the promoted type of the element products and converts to @c T
1090 /// once on return, so e.g. @c Vec3i::dot(Vec3d) does not truncate partial sums.
1091 template<typename V>
1092 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr T dot(const V& v) const noexcept {
1093 auto s = mVec[0] * v[0];
1094 for (int i = 1; i < N; ++i) s += mVec[i] * v[i];
1095 return T(s);
1096 }
1097 /// @brief Squared L2 length (sum of squared components). Constexpr, no sqrt.
1098 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr T lengthSqr() const noexcept {
1099 auto s = mVec[0] * mVec[0];
1100 for (int i = 1; i < N; ++i) s += mVec[i] * mVec[i];
1101 return T(s);
1102 }
1103 /// @brief L2 length (Euclidean norm). Not @c constexpr — calls @c Sqrt.
1104 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] T length() const noexcept { return Sqrt(this->lengthSqr()); }
1105
1106 /// @brief return the smallest of the N components
1107 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr T smallestComponent() const noexcept {
1108 T m = mVec[0];
1109 for (int i = 1; i < N; ++i) if (mVec[i] < m) m = mVec[i];
1110 return m;
1111 }
1112 /// @brief return the largest of the N components
1113 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr T largestComponent() const noexcept {
1114 T m = mVec[0];
1115 for (int i = 1; i < N; ++i) if (mVec[i] > m) m = mVec[i];
1116 return m;
1117 }
1118
1119 // ---- component-wise (mutating) min/max ----
1120
1121 /// @brief Component-wise take the @c min of @c *this and @a other (in place); return @c *this.
1122 template<typename V>
1123 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& mergeMin(const V& other) noexcept {
1124 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) if (other[i] < mVec[i]) mVec[i] = other[i];
1125 return *this;
1126 }
1127 /// @brief Component-wise take the @c max of @c *this and @a other (in place); return @c *this.
1128 template<typename V>
1129 __hostdev__ constexpr VecBase& mergeMax(const V& other) noexcept {
1130 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) if (other[i] > mVec[i]) mVec[i] = other[i];
1131 return *this;
1132 }
1133
1134 // ---- integer rounding (toward -inf / +inf / nearest) ----
1135 //
1136
1137 /// @brief floor-rounded components into the @c Result type (whose @c [i]
1138 /// must accept int32_t). For integer @c T the value is passed through.
1139 /// @note Only the integer-@c T specialization is usable as a constant
1140 /// expression; the floating-point branch calls @c math::Floor, which
1141 /// isn't constexpr until C++23.
1142 template<typename Result>
1143 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Result floorAs() const noexcept {
1144 Result r{};
1145 if constexpr (std::is_floating_point<T>::value) {
1146 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) r[i] = math::Floor(mVec[i]);
1147 } else {
1148 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) r[i] = static_cast<int32_t>(mVec[i]);
1149 }
1150 return r;
1151 }
1152 /// @brief ceil-rounded components into the @c Result type (whose @c [i]
1153 /// must accept int32_t). For integer @c T the value is passed through.
1154 /// @note Only the integer-@c T specialization is usable as a constant
1155 /// expression; the floating-point branch calls @c math::Ceil, which
1156 /// isn't constexpr until C++23.
1157 template<typename Result>
1158 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Result ceilAs() const noexcept {
1159 Result r{};
1160 if constexpr (std::is_floating_point<T>::value) {
1161 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) r[i] = math::Ceil(mVec[i]);
1162 } else {
1163 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) r[i] = static_cast<int32_t>(mVec[i]);
1164 }
1165 return r;
1166 }
1167 /// @brief nearest-integer rounding for floating @c T via the scalar
1168 /// @c math::Round (halfway cases toward +inf, exact for every input), so
1169 /// float and double agree; pass-through for integer @c T.
1170 /// @note See @c floorAs — only the integer-@c T branch is constexpr-usable.
1171 template<typename Result>
1172 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Result roundAs() const noexcept {
1173 Result r{};
1174 if constexpr (std::is_floating_point<T>::value) {
1175 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) r[i] = math::Round(mVec[i]);
1176 } else {
1177 for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) r[i] = static_cast<int32_t>(mVec[i]);
1178 }
1179 return r;
1180 }
1181}; // VecBase<T, N>
1182
1183// ----------------------------> Vec2 <--------------------------------------
1184
1185/// @brief A simple vector class with two components, similar to openvdb::math::Vec2
1186///
1187/// Naturally aligned (@c alignof(T)), like all Vec/Mat classes. Raising the
1188/// alignment would change the layout of every struct and buffer that holds one;
1189/// use @c Vec2Aligned for over-aligned arrays.
1190template<typename T>
1191class Vec2 : public VecBase<T, 2>
1192{
1193 using Base = VecBase<T, 2>;
1194
1195public:
1196 using ValueType = T;
1197 static constexpr int size = 2; // openvdb::math::Tuple-compat alias of SIZE
1198
1199 /// @brief Default-construct (components are left uninitialized for fundamental @c T).
1200 Vec2() noexcept = default;
1201 /// @brief Broadcast: set both components to @a x.
1202 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec2(T x) noexcept : Base(x, x) {}
1203 /// @brief Component-wise construction.
1204 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2(T x, T y) noexcept : Base(x, y) {}
1205
1206 /// @brief Explicit cross-template converting ctor (e.g. from @c openvdb::Vec2).
1207 /// Convert a foreign vector with a cast, e.g. @c Vec2<float>(v).
1208 template<template<class> class Vec2T, class T2>
1209 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec2(const Vec2T<T2>& v) noexcept : Base(v[0], v[1])
1210 {
1211 static_assert(Vec2T<T2>::size == 2, "expected Vec2T::size==2!");
1212 }
1213 /// @brief Explicit cross-precision conversion within nanovdb (e.g. @c Vec2d → @c Vec2f).
1214 template<typename T2>
1215 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec2(const Vec2<T2>& v) noexcept : Base(v[0], v[1]) {}
1216 /// @brief Construct from a 2D integer coordinate.
1217 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec2(const Coord2& ijk) noexcept : Base(ijk[0], ijk[1]) {}
1218
1219 /// @brief Assign from any 2-component vector type (foreign or nanovdb).
1220 template<template<class> class Vec2T, class T2>
1221 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& operator=(const Vec2T<T2>& rhs) noexcept {
1222 static_assert(Vec2T<T2>::size == 2, "expected Vec2T::size==2!");
1223 this->mVec[0] = rhs[0]; this->mVec[1] = rhs[1];
1224 return *this;
1225 }
1226
1227 // ---- element-wise (Vec & Vec) ----
1228 /// @brief Component-wise negation.
1229 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator-() const noexcept { return Base::template negate<Vec2>(); }
1230 /// @brief Component-wise sum.
1231 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator+(const Vec2& v) const noexcept { return Base::template plus<Vec2>(v); }
1232 /// @brief Component-wise difference.
1233 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator-(const Vec2& v) const noexcept { return Base::template minus<Vec2>(v); }
1234 /// @brief Component-wise (Hadamard) product.
1235 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator*(const Vec2& v) const noexcept { return Base::template mul<Vec2>(v); }
1236 /// @brief Component-wise division.
1237 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator/(const Vec2& v) const noexcept { return Base::template div<Vec2>(v); }
1238 /// @brief In-place component-wise addition.
1239 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& operator+=(const Vec2& v) noexcept { Base::addAssign(v); return *this; }
1240 /// @brief In-place component-wise subtraction.
1241 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& operator-=(const Vec2& v) noexcept { Base::subAssign(v); return *this; }
1242
1243 // ---- mixed Vec2 / Coord2 ----
1244 /// @brief Add an integer @c Coord2 to this vector (component-wise).
1245 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator+(const Coord2& ijk) const noexcept { return Vec2(this->mVec[0] + ijk[0], this->mVec[1] + ijk[1]); }
1246 /// @brief Subtract an integer @c Coord2 from this vector (component-wise).
1247 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator-(const Coord2& ijk) const noexcept { return Vec2(this->mVec[0] - ijk[0], this->mVec[1] - ijk[1]); }
1248 /// @brief In-place component-wise addition of an integer @c Coord2.
1249 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& operator+=(const Coord2& ijk) noexcept {
1250 this->mVec[0] += T(ijk[0]); this->mVec[1] += T(ijk[1]);
1251 return *this;
1252 }
1253 /// @brief In-place component-wise subtraction of an integer @c Coord2.
1254 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& operator-=(const Coord2& ijk) noexcept {
1255 this->mVec[0] -= T(ijk[0]); this->mVec[1] -= T(ijk[1]);
1256 return *this;
1257 }
1258
1259 // ---- scalar ----
1260 /// @brief Component-wise multiply by scalar @a s.
1261 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator*(const T& s) const noexcept { return Base::template scale<Vec2>(s); }
1262 /// @brief Component-wise divide by scalar @a s (integer-safe).
1263 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2 operator/(const T& s) const noexcept { return Base::template divideBy<Vec2>(s); }
1264 /// @brief In-place component-wise multiply by scalar @a s.
1265 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& operator*=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::scaleAssign(s); return *this; }
1266 /// @brief In-place component-wise divide by scalar @a s.
1267 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& operator/=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::divideAssignScalar(s); return *this; }
1268 /// @brief Normalize in place (divide by @c length()). Not @c constexpr — calls @c std::sqrt.
1269 __hostdev__ Vec2& normalize() noexcept { return (*this) /= this->length(); }
1270 /// @brief Return a normalized (unit-length) copy; const counterpart of @c normalize().
1271 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] Vec2 normalized() const noexcept {
1272 return Base::template normalized<Vec2>();
1273 }
1274
1275 // ---- equality ----
1276 /// @brief Component-wise equality.
1277 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const Vec2& rhs) const noexcept { return Base::equals(rhs); }
1278 /// @brief Component-wise inequality.
1279 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const Vec2& rhs) const noexcept { return !Base::equals(rhs); }
1280
1281 // ---- component-wise min/max ----
1282 /// @brief Take the component-wise minimum of @c *this and @a other in place.
1283 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& minComponent(const Vec2& other) noexcept { Base::mergeMin(other); return *this; }
1284 /// @brief Take the component-wise maximum of @c *this and @a other in place.
1285 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2& maxComponent(const Vec2& other) noexcept { Base::mergeMax(other); return *this; }
1286
1287 /// @brief Return the smallest vector component
1288 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr ValueType min() const noexcept { return Base::smallestComponent(); }
1289 /// @brief Return the largest vector component
1290 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr ValueType max() const noexcept { return Base::largestComponent(); }
1291
1292 /// @brief Round each component down (toward negative infinity)
1293 /// @return integer Coord2
1294 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (floorAs uses non-constexpr math::Floor for floating point).
1295 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 floor() const noexcept { return Base::template floorAs<Coord2>(); }
1296 /// @brief Round each component up (toward positive infinity)
1297 /// @return integer Coord2
1298 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (ceilAs uses non-constexpr math::Ceil for floating point).
1299 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 ceil() const noexcept { return Base::template ceilAs<Coord2>(); }
1300 /// @brief Round each component to its closest integer value
1301 /// @return integer Coord2
1302 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (roundAs uses non-constexpr math::Round for floating point).
1303 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord2 round() const noexcept { return Base::template roundAs<Coord2>(); }
1304
1305 // ---- scalar * Vec / scalar / Vec (hidden friends — found only via ADL on Vec2,
1306 // never participate in unrelated namespace-scope overload sets) ----
1307
1308 /// @brief Scalar-on-the-left multiplication (hidden friend).
1309 template<typename T1>
1310 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr Vec2 operator*(T1 scalar, const Vec2& vec) noexcept
1311 {
1312 return Vec2(scalar * vec[0], scalar * vec[1]);
1313 }
1314 /// @brief Scalar-on-the-left division (hidden friend).
1315 template<typename T1>
1316 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr Vec2 operator/(T1 scalar, const Vec2& vec) noexcept
1317 {
1318 return Vec2(scalar / vec[0], scalar / vec[1]);
1319 }
1320}; // Vec2<T>
1321
1322/// @brief Return a single precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
1323__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec2<float> Coord2::asVec2s() const noexcept
1324{
1325 return Vec2<float>(float(mVec[0]), float(mVec[1]));
1326}
1327
1328/// @brief Return a double precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
1329__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec2<double> Coord2::asVec2d() const noexcept
1330{
1331 return Vec2<double>(double(mVec[0]), double(mVec[1]));
1332}

1334
1335/// @brief Base class for fixed-size matrices. Provides shared element-wise
1336/// arithmetic, scalar arithmetic, equality, transpose, mat*mat, and mat*vec.
1337/// Storage is a flat row-major array @c mData[ROWS * COLS]. Derived classes
1338/// supply constructors plus any dimension-specific extras (e.g. @c inverse()
1339/// on @c Mat2).
1340template<typename T, int ROWS, int COLS>
1341class MatBase {
1342protected:
1343 T mData[ROWS * COLS]; // 1D array storage
1344
1345public:
1346 using ValueType = T;
1347
1348 /// @brief Compile-time row count.
1349 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr int rows() noexcept { return ROWS; }
1350 /// @brief Compile-time column count.
1351 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr int cols() noexcept { return COLS; }
1352 /// @brief Compile-time element count, i.e. @c ROWS * @c COLS.
1353 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr int size() noexcept { return ROWS * COLS; }
1354
1355 /// @brief Default-construct (entries are left uninitialized for trivially-default-constructible @c T).
1356 MatBase() noexcept = default;
1357
1358 /// @brief Read @c ROWS*COLS elements from @a array in row-major order, converting each
1359 /// element from @c S to @c T via @c static_cast.
1360 template<typename S>
1361 __hostdev__ constexpr MatBase(S* array) noexcept {
1362 for (int i = 0; i < size(); ++i) {
1363 mData[i] = static_cast<T>(array[i]);
1364 }
1365 }
1366
1367protected:
1368 /// @brief Variadic component-init ctor — used only by derived ctors
1369 /// (`Mat2(T a, T b, T c, T d) : Base(a, b, c, d) {}`). The member-init
1370 /// list directly initializes @c mData, avoiding the default-construct-
1371 /// then-assign that a body-assignment ctor would impose on a
1372 /// non-fundamental @c T.
1373 template<typename... Args>
1374 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr MatBase(Args... args) noexcept : mData{T(args)...}
1375 {
1376 static_assert(sizeof...(Args) == ROWS * COLS, "MatBase: wrong number of constructor arguments");
1377 }
1378
1379 /// @brief Return a @c Result whose row-major element @c idx is @c f(idx), built
1380 /// through its @a Count-element constructor. This is constexpr-valid in C++17
1381 /// without first value-initializing a result and overwriting it.
1382 template<typename Result, typename F, int... I>
1383 __hostdev__ static constexpr Result generate(F f, std::integer_sequence<int, I...>) noexcept
1384 {
1385 return Result(typename Result::ValueType(f(I))...);
1386 }
1387 template<typename Result, int Count = ROWS * COLS, typename F>
1388 __hostdev__ static constexpr Result generate(F f) noexcept
1389 {
1390 return generate<Result>(f, std::make_integer_sequence<int, Count>{});
1391 }
1392
1393public:
1394
1395 /// @brief 2D row access. Returns a pointer to the start of @a row; the caller
1396 /// indexes into it with the column. Asserts @c 0 <= @a row < @c ROWS in debug
1397 /// builds; column index is the caller's responsibility (use @c 0 <= col < @c COLS).
1398 __hostdev__ constexpr T* operator[](int row) noexcept {
1399 NANOVDB_ASSERT(row >= 0 && row < ROWS);
1400 return &mData[row * COLS];
1401 }
1402 /// @brief Const overload of @c operator[](int); see non-const variant.
1403 __hostdev__ constexpr const T* operator[](int row) const noexcept {
1404 NANOVDB_ASSERT(row >= 0 && row < ROWS);
1405 return &mData[row * COLS];
1406 }
1407
1408 /// @brief return a raw pointer to the underlying 1D storage (row-major)
1409 __hostdev__ constexpr T* data() noexcept { return mData; }
1410 /// @brief return a const raw pointer to the underlying 1D storage (row-major)
1411 __hostdev__ constexpr const T* data() const noexcept { return mData; }
1412
1413 // ---- generic element-wise helpers ----
1414
1415 /// @brief return @c *this + @a rhs as a @c Derived
1416 template<typename Derived>
1417 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived plus(const Derived& rhs) const noexcept {
1418 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mData[i] + rhs.data()[i]; });
1419 }
1420
1421 /// @brief return @c *this - @a rhs as a @c Derived
1422 template<typename Derived>
1423 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived minus(const Derived& rhs) const noexcept {
1424 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mData[i] - rhs.data()[i]; });
1425 }
1426
1427 /// @brief return -(*this) as a @c Derived
1428 template<typename Derived>
1429 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived negate() const noexcept {
1430 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return -mData[i]; });
1431 }
1432
1433 /// @brief return @a s * (*this) as a @c Derived
1434 template<typename Derived>
1435 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived scale(T s) const noexcept {
1436 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mData[i] * s; });
1437 }
1438
1439 /// @brief Element-wise add @a rhs into @c *this and return @c *this.
1440 __hostdev__ constexpr MatBase& addAssign(const MatBase& rhs) noexcept {
1441 for (int i = 0; i < size(); ++i) mData[i] += rhs.mData[i];
1442 return *this;
1443 }
1444 /// @brief Element-wise subtract @a rhs from @c *this and return @c *this.
1445 __hostdev__ constexpr MatBase& subAssign(const MatBase& rhs) noexcept {
1446 for (int i = 0; i < size(); ++i) mData[i] -= rhs.mData[i];
1447 return *this;
1448 }
1449 /// @brief Multiply every element by scalar @a s in place; return @c *this.
1450 /// @a s is taken by value so @c m *= m[0][0] scales every element by the original value.
1451 __hostdev__ constexpr MatBase& scaleAssign(T s) noexcept {
1452 for (int i = 0; i < size(); ++i) mData[i] *= s;
1453 return *this;
1454 }
1455
1456 /// @brief return (*this) / @a s element-wise as a @c Derived. Floating-point
1457 /// @c T multiplies by the reciprocal @c 1/s; integer @c T divides each element,
1458 /// since @c 1/s would truncate to zero.
1459 template<typename Derived>
1460 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Derived divideBy(T s) const noexcept {
1461 if constexpr (std::is_floating_point<T>::value) {
1462 return this->template scale<Derived>(T(1) / s);
1463 } else {
1464 return generate<Derived>([&](int i) { return mData[i] / s; });
1465 }
1466 }
1467 /// @brief Divide every element by scalar @a s in place; return @c *this.
1468 /// Uses the same floating-point reciprocal / integer per-element split as
1469 /// @c divideBy. @a s is taken by value so @c m /= m[0][0] is safe.
1470 __hostdev__ constexpr MatBase& divideAssignScalar(T s) noexcept {
1471 if constexpr (std::is_floating_point<T>::value) {
1472 return this->scaleAssign(T(1) / s);
1473 } else {
1474 for (int i = 0; i < size(); ++i) mData[i] /= s;
1475 return *this;
1476 }
1477 }
1478
1479 /// @brief Return @c true iff every element compares equal to @a rhs.
1480 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool equals(const MatBase& rhs) const noexcept {
1481 for (int i = 0; i < size(); ++i) if (mData[i] != rhs.mData[i]) return false;
1482 return true;
1483 }
1484
1485 // ---- generic transpose ----
1486
1487 /// @brief return the transpose of @c *this as the @c Result type.
1488 /// @tparam Result a matrix type whose dimensions are (COLS, ROWS)
1489 template<typename Result>
1490 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Result transposeAs() const noexcept {
1491 static_assert(Result::rows() == COLS && Result::cols() == ROWS,
1492 "transposeAs: result dims must be (COLS, ROWS)");
1493 // Result element (j, i) sits at row-major index j * ROWS + i.
1494 return generate<Result>([&](int idx) { return mData[(idx % ROWS) * COLS + idx / ROWS]; });
1495 }
1496
1497 // ---- generic matrix * matrix ----
1498
1499 /// @brief return (*this) * @a rhs as the @c Result type.
1500 /// @tparam Result a matrix type whose dimensions are (ROWS, Rhs::cols())
1501 /// @tparam Rhs a matrix type whose row count equals @c COLS
1502 template<typename Result, typename Rhs>
1503 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Result multiply(const Rhs& rhs) const noexcept {
1504 static_assert(COLS == Rhs::rows(), "multiply: lhs.cols must equal rhs.rows");
1505 static_assert(Result::rows() == ROWS && Result::cols() == Rhs::cols(),
1506 "multiply: result dims mismatch");
1507 return generate<Result, ROWS * Rhs::cols()>([&](int idx) {
1508 const int i = idx / Rhs::cols(), j = idx % Rhs::cols();
1509 T sum = mData[i * COLS] * rhs[0][j];
1510 for (int k = 1; k < COLS; ++k) sum += mData[i * COLS + k] * rhs[k][j];
1511 return sum;
1512 });
1513 }
1514
1515 // ---- generic matrix * vector ----
1516
1517 /// @brief return (*this) * @a v as the @c VecResult type.
1518 /// @tparam VecResult a vector type whose @c SIZE equals @c ROWS
1519 /// @tparam VecRhs a vector type whose @c SIZE equals @c COLS
1520 template<typename VecResult, typename VecRhs>
1521 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr VecResult multiplyVec(const VecRhs& v) const noexcept {
1522 static_assert(VecRhs::SIZE == COLS && VecResult::SIZE == ROWS,
1523 "multiplyVec: dim mismatch");
1524 return generate<VecResult, ROWS>([&](int i) {
1525 T sum = mData[i * COLS] * v[0];
1526 for (int k = 1; k < COLS; ++k) sum += mData[i * COLS + k] * v[k];
1527 return sum;
1528 });
1529 }
1530};
1531
1532// Forward declarations
1533template<typename T> class Mat2;
1534template<typename T> class Mat2x3;
1535template<typename T> class Mat3x2;
1536template<typename T> class Mat3;
1537template<typename T> class Mat4;
1538template<typename T> class Vec4;
1539
1540
1541
1542/// @brief 2x2 row-major matrix.
1543/// @details Naturally aligned (@c alignof(T)), like all Vec/Mat classes, so the
1544/// layout of structs and buffers that hold one does not depend on this class.
1545template <typename T>
1546class Mat2 : public MatBase<T, 2, 2> {
1547 using Base = MatBase<T, 2, 2>;
1548public:
1549 /// @brief Default-construct (entries left uninitialized for fundamental @c T).
1550 Mat2() noexcept = default;
1551 /// @brief Constructor given individual array elements, the ordering is in row major form:
1552 /** @verbatim
1553 a b
1554 c d
1555 @endverbatim */
1556 __hostdev__ constexpr Mat2(T a, T b, T c, T d) noexcept : Base(a, b, c, d) {}
1557
1558 /// @brief Constructor given array of elements, the ordering is in row major form
1559 template<typename Source>
1560 __hostdev__ constexpr Mat2(Source* array) noexcept : Base(array) {}
1561
1562 // ---- element-wise ----
1563 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2 operator-() const noexcept { return this->template negate<Mat2>(); }
1564 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2 operator+(const Mat2& m) const noexcept { return this->template plus<Mat2>(m); }
1565 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2 operator-(const Mat2& m) const noexcept { return this->template minus<Mat2>(m); }
1566 __hostdev__ constexpr Mat2& operator+=(const Mat2& m) noexcept { Base::addAssign(m); return *this; }
1567 __hostdev__ constexpr Mat2& operator-=(const Mat2& m) noexcept { Base::subAssign(m); return *this; }
1568
1569 // ---- matrix * matrix / matrix * vector ----
1570 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2 operator*(const Mat2& m) const noexcept { return this->template multiply<Mat2, Mat2>(m); }
1571 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec2<T> operator*(const Vec2<T>& v) const noexcept { return this->template multiplyVec<Vec2<T>, Vec2<T>>(v); }
1572
1573 // ---- scalar ----
1574 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2 operator*(const T& s) const noexcept { return this->template scale<Mat2>(s); }
1575 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2 operator/(const T& s) const noexcept { return this->template divideBy<Mat2>(s); }
1576 __hostdev__ constexpr Mat2& operator*=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::scaleAssign(s); return *this; }
1577 __hostdev__ constexpr Mat2& operator/=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::divideAssignScalar(s); return *this; }
1578
1579 // ---- equality ----
1580 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const Mat2& m) const noexcept { return Base::equals(m); }
1581 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const Mat2& m) const noexcept { return !Base::equals(m); }
1582
1583 /// @brief returns transpose of this
1584 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2 transpose() const noexcept { return this->template transposeAs<Mat2>(); }
1585
1586 /// @brief returns inverse of this
1587 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat2<T> inverse() const noexcept {
1588 T det = (*this)[0][0] * (*this)[1][1] - (*this)[0][1] * (*this)[1][0];
1589 if (isApproxZero(det)) {
1590 return Mat2<T>(T(0), T(0), T(0), T(0));
1591 }
1592 T invDet = T(1) / det;
1593 return Mat2<T>((*this)[1][1] * invDet, -(*this)[0][1] * invDet,
1594 -(*this)[1][0] * invDet, (*this)[0][0] * invDet);
1595 }
1596
1597 /// @brief scalar * Mat (hidden friend — found only via ADL on Mat2)
1598 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr Mat2 operator*(const T& s, const Mat2& m) noexcept {
1599 return m.template scale<Mat2>(s);
1600 }
1601};
1602
1603/// @brief 2x3 row-major matrix.
1604/// @details Intentionally NOT @c alignas-elevated: its byte size
1605/// (6*sizeof(T)) is not a power-of-2 multiple of @c alignof(T), so any
1606/// @c alignas(N > alignof(T)) would force tail padding and break
1607/// packed-array layout plus on-disk format compatibility.
1608template <typename T>
1609class Mat2x3 : public MatBase<T, 2, 3> {

1856/// @brief A simple vector class with three components, similar to openvdb::math::Vec3
1857///
1858/// Vec3 is intentionally NOT alignas-elevated: its byte size
1859/// (3*sizeof(T)) is not a power-of-2 multiple of alignof(T), so any
1860/// alignas(N > alignof(T)) would force tail padding and break
1861/// packed-array layout plus on-disk format compatibility. Use @c Vec3Aligned
1862/// for padded, over-aligned user arrays.
1863template<typename T>
1864class Vec3 : public VecBase<T, 3>
1865{
1866 using Base = VecBase<T, 3>;
1867
1868public:
1869 using ValueType = T;
1870 static constexpr int size = 3; // openvdb::math::Tuple-compat alias of SIZE
1871
1872 /// @brief Default-construct (components are left uninitialized for fundamental @c T).
1873 Vec3() noexcept = default;
1874 /// @brief Broadcast: set all three components to @a x.
1875 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec3(T x) noexcept : Base(x, x, x) {}
1876 /// @brief Component-wise construction.
1877 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3(T x, T y, T z) noexcept : Base(x, y, z) {}
1878
1879 /// @brief Explicit cross-template converting ctor (e.g. from @c openvdb::Vec3).
1880 /// Convert a foreign vector with a cast, e.g. @c Vec3<float>(v).
1881 template<template<class> class Vec3T, class T2>
1882 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec3(const Vec3T<T2>& v) noexcept : Base(v[0], v[1], v[2])
1883 {
1884 static_assert(Vec3T<T2>::size == 3, "expected Vec3T::size==3!");
1885 }
1886 /// @brief Explicit cross-precision conversion within nanovdb (e.g. @c Vec3d → @c Vec3f).
1887 template<typename T2>
1888 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec3(const Vec3<T2>& v) noexcept : Base(v[0], v[1], v[2]) {}
1889 /// @brief Construct from a 3D integer coordinate.
1890 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec3(const Coord& ijk) noexcept : Base(ijk[0], ijk[1], ijk[2]) {}
1891
1892 /// @brief Assign from any 3-component vector type (foreign or nanovdb).
1893 template<template<class> class Vec3T, class T2>
1894 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& operator=(const Vec3T<T2>& rhs) noexcept {
1895 static_assert(Vec3T<T2>::size == 3, "expected Vec3T::size==3!");
1896 this->mVec[0] = rhs[0]; this->mVec[1] = rhs[1]; this->mVec[2] = rhs[2];
1897 return *this;
1898 }
1899
1900 // ---- element-wise (Vec & Vec) ----
1901 /// @brief Component-wise negation.
1902 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator-() const noexcept { return Base::template negate<Vec3>(); }
1903 /// @brief Component-wise sum.
1904 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator+(const Vec3& v) const noexcept { return Base::template plus<Vec3>(v); }
1905 /// @brief Component-wise difference.
1906 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator-(const Vec3& v) const noexcept { return Base::template minus<Vec3>(v); }
1907 /// @brief Component-wise (Hadamard) product.
1908 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator*(const Vec3& v) const noexcept { return Base::template mul<Vec3>(v); }
1909 /// @brief Component-wise division.
1910 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator/(const Vec3& v) const noexcept { return Base::template div<Vec3>(v); }
1911 /// @brief In-place component-wise addition.
1912 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& operator+=(const Vec3& v) noexcept { Base::addAssign(v); return *this; }
1913 /// @brief In-place component-wise subtraction.
1914 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& operator-=(const Vec3& v) noexcept { Base::subAssign(v); return *this; }
1915
1916 // ---- mixed Vec3 / Coord (3D) ----
1917 /// @brief Add an integer @c Coord to this vector (component-wise).
1918 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator+(const Coord& ijk) const noexcept { return Vec3(this->mVec[0] + T(ijk[0]), this->mVec[1] + T(ijk[1]), this->mVec[2] + T(ijk[2])); }
1919 /// @brief Subtract an integer @c Coord from this vector (component-wise).
1920 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator-(const Coord& ijk) const noexcept { return Vec3(this->mVec[0] - T(ijk[0]), this->mVec[1] - T(ijk[1]), this->mVec[2] - T(ijk[2])); }
1921 /// @brief In-place component-wise addition of an integer @c Coord.
1922 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& operator+=(const Coord& ijk) noexcept {
1923 this->mVec[0] += T(ijk[0]); this->mVec[1] += T(ijk[1]); this->mVec[2] += T(ijk[2]);
1924 return *this;
1925 }
1926 /// @brief In-place component-wise subtraction of an integer @c Coord.
1927 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& operator-=(const Coord& ijk) noexcept {
1928 this->mVec[0] -= T(ijk[0]); this->mVec[1] -= T(ijk[1]); this->mVec[2] -= T(ijk[2]);
1929 return *this;
1930 }
1931
1932 // ---- scalar ----
1933 /// @brief Component-wise multiply by scalar @a s.
1934 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator*(const T& s) const noexcept { return Base::template scale<Vec3>(s); }
1935 /// @brief Component-wise divide by scalar @a s (integer-safe).
1936 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 operator/(const T& s) const noexcept { return Base::template divideBy<Vec3>(s); }
1937 /// @brief In-place component-wise multiply by scalar @a s.
1938 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& operator*=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::scaleAssign(s); return *this; }
1939 /// @brief In-place component-wise divide by scalar @a s.
1940 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& operator/=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::divideAssignScalar(s); return *this; }
1941 /// @brief Normalize in place (divide by @c length()). Not @c constexpr — calls @c std::sqrt.
1942 __hostdev__ Vec3& normalize() noexcept { return (*this) /= this->length(); }
1943 /// @brief Return a normalized (unit-length) copy; const counterpart of @c normalize().
1944 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] Vec3 normalized() const noexcept {
1945 return Base::template normalized<Vec3>();
1946 }
1947
1948 // ---- equality ----
1949 /// @brief Component-wise equality.
1950 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const Vec3& rhs) const noexcept { return Base::equals(rhs); }
1951 /// @brief Component-wise inequality.
1952 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const Vec3& rhs) const noexcept { return !Base::equals(rhs); }
1953
1954 // ---- component-wise min/max ----
1955 /// @brief Take the component-wise minimum of @c *this and @a other in place.
1956 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& minComponent(const Vec3& other) noexcept { Base::mergeMin(other); return *this; }
1957 /// @brief Take the component-wise maximum of @c *this and @a other in place.
1958 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3& maxComponent(const Vec3& other) noexcept { Base::mergeMax(other); return *this; }
1959
1960 /// @brief Return the smallest vector component
1961 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr ValueType min() const noexcept { return Base::smallestComponent(); }
1962 /// @brief Return the largest vector component
1963 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr ValueType max() const noexcept { return Base::largestComponent(); }
1964
1965 /// @brief Round each component down (toward negative infinity)
1966 /// @return integer Coord
1967 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (floorAs uses non-constexpr math::Floor for floating point).
1968 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord floor() const noexcept { return Base::template floorAs<Coord>(); }
1969 /// @brief Round each component up (toward positive infinity)
1970 /// @return integer Coord
1971 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (ceilAs uses non-constexpr math::Ceil for floating point).
1972 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord ceil() const noexcept { return Base::template ceilAs<Coord>(); }
1973 /// @brief Round each component to its closest integer value
1974 /// @return integer Coord
1975 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (roundAs uses non-constexpr math::Round for floating point).
1976 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Coord round() const noexcept { return Base::template roundAs<Coord>(); }
1977
1978 // ---- 3D-specific ----
1979
1980 /// @brief cross product with another 3-vector
1981 template<typename Vec3T>
1982 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec3 cross(const Vec3T& v) const noexcept {
1983 return Vec3(this->mVec[1] * v[2] - this->mVec[2] * v[1],
1984 this->mVec[2] * v[0] - this->mVec[0] * v[2],
1985 this->mVec[0] * v[1] - this->mVec[1] * v[0]);
1986 }
1987
1988 /// @brief Outer product of a 3x1 vector and a 1x3 vector, result is a 3x3 matrix
1989 template<typename Vec3T>
1990 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Mat3<ValueType> outer(const Vec3T& v) const noexcept {
1991 return Mat3<ValueType>(this->mVec[0] * v[0], this->mVec[0] * v[1], this->mVec[0] * v[2],
1992 this->mVec[1] * v[0], this->mVec[1] * v[1], this->mVec[1] * v[2],
1993 this->mVec[2] * v[0], this->mVec[2] * v[1], this->mVec[2] * v[2]);
1994 }
1995
1996 // ---- scalar * Vec / scalar / Vec (hidden friends — found only via ADL on Vec3,
1997 // never participate in unrelated namespace-scope overload sets) ----
1998
1999 /// @brief Scalar-on-the-left multiplication (hidden friend).
2000 template<typename T1>
2001 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr Vec3 operator*(T1 scalar, const Vec3& vec) noexcept
2002 {
2003 return Vec3(T(scalar * vec[0]), T(scalar * vec[1]), T(scalar * vec[2]));
2004 }
2005 /// @brief Scalar-on-the-left division (hidden friend).
2006 template<typename T1>
2007 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr Vec3 operator/(T1 scalar, const Vec3& vec) noexcept
2008 {
2009 return Vec3(T(scalar / vec[0]), T(scalar / vec[1]), T(scalar / vec[2]));
2010 }
2011}; // Vec3<T>

2013/// @brief Return a single precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
2014__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3<float> Coord::asVec3s() const noexcept
2015{
2016 return Vec3<float>(float(mVec[0]), float(mVec[1]), float(mVec[2]));
2017}
2018
2019/// @brief Return a double precision floating-point vector of this coordinate
2020__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3<double> Coord::asVec3d() const noexcept
2021{
2022 return Vec3<double>(double(mVec[0]), double(mVec[1]), double(mVec[2]));
2023}
