2025// ----------------------------> Vec4 <--------------------------------------
2026
2027/// @brief A simple vector class with four components, similar to openvdb::math::Vec4
2028///
2029/// Naturally aligned (@c alignof(T)). @c Vec4 is a grid value type, so its
2030/// alignment sets field offsets in the NanoVDB file format and in PNanoVDB.
2031/// Use @c Vec4Aligned for over-aligned user arrays.
2032template<typename T>
2033class Vec4 : public VecBase<T, 4>
2034{
2035 using Base = VecBase<T, 4>;
2036
2037public:
2038 using ValueType = T;
2039 static constexpr int size = 4; // openvdb::math::Tuple-compat alias of SIZE
2040
2041 /// @brief Default-construct (components are left uninitialized for fundamental @c T).
2042 Vec4() noexcept = default;
2043 /// @brief Broadcast: set all four components to @a x.
2044 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec4(T x) noexcept : Base(x, x, x, x) {}
2045 /// @brief Component-wise construction.
2046 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4(T x, T y, T z, T w) noexcept : Base(x, y, z, w) {}
2047
2048 /// @brief Explicit cross-precision conversion within nanovdb (e.g. @c Vec4d → @c Vec4f).
2049 template<typename T2>
2050 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec4(const Vec4<T2>& v) noexcept : Base(v[0], v[1], v[2], v[3]) {}
2051 /// @brief Explicit cross-template converting ctor (e.g. from @c openvdb::Vec4).
2052 /// Convert a foreign vector with a cast, e.g. @c Vec4<float>(v).
2053 template<template<class> class Vec4T, class T2>
2054 __hostdev__ explicit constexpr Vec4(const Vec4T<T2>& v) noexcept : Base(v[0], v[1], v[2], v[3])
2055 {
2056 static_assert(Vec4T<T2>::size == 4, "expected Vec4T::size==4!");
2057 }
2058 /// @brief Assign from any 4-component vector type (foreign or nanovdb).
2059 template<template<class> class Vec4T, class T2>
2060 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4& operator=(const Vec4T<T2>& rhs) noexcept {
2061 static_assert(Vec4T<T2>::size == 4, "expected Vec4T::size==4!");
2062 this->mVec[0] = rhs[0]; this->mVec[1] = rhs[1]; this->mVec[2] = rhs[2]; this->mVec[3] = rhs[3];
2063 return *this;
2064 }
2065
2066 // ---- element-wise (Vec & Vec) ----
2067 /// @brief Component-wise negation.
2068 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4 operator-() const noexcept { return Base::template negate<Vec4>(); }
2069 /// @brief Component-wise sum.
2070 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4 operator+(const Vec4& v) const noexcept { return Base::template plus<Vec4>(v); }
2071 /// @brief Component-wise difference.
2072 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4 operator-(const Vec4& v) const noexcept { return Base::template minus<Vec4>(v); }
2073 /// @brief Component-wise (Hadamard) product.
2074 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4 operator*(const Vec4& v) const noexcept { return Base::template mul<Vec4>(v); }
2075 /// @brief Component-wise division.
2076 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4 operator/(const Vec4& v) const noexcept { return Base::template div<Vec4>(v); }
2077 /// @brief In-place component-wise addition.
2078 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4& operator+=(const Vec4& v) noexcept { Base::addAssign(v); return *this; }
2079 /// @brief In-place component-wise subtraction.
2080 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4& operator-=(const Vec4& v) noexcept { Base::subAssign(v); return *this; }
2081
2082 // ---- scalar ----
2083 /// @brief Component-wise multiply by scalar @a s.
2084 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4 operator*(const T& s) const noexcept { return Base::template scale<Vec4>(s); }
2085 /// @brief Component-wise divide by scalar @a s (integer-safe).
2086 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4 operator/(const T& s) const noexcept { return Base::template divideBy<Vec4>(s); }
2087 /// @brief In-place component-wise multiply by scalar @a s.
2088 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4& operator*=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::scaleAssign(s); return *this; }
2089 /// @brief In-place component-wise divide by scalar @a s.
2090 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4& operator/=(const T& s) noexcept { Base::divideAssignScalar(s); return *this; }
2091 /// @brief Normalize in place (divide by @c length()). Not @c constexpr — calls @c std::sqrt.
2092 __hostdev__ Vec4& normalize() noexcept { return (*this) /= this->length(); }
2093 /// @brief Return a normalized (unit-length) copy; const counterpart of @c normalize().
2094 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] Vec4 normalized() const noexcept {
2095 return Base::template normalized<Vec4>();
2096 }
2097
2098 // ---- equality ----
2099 /// @brief Component-wise equality.
2100 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const Vec4& rhs) const noexcept { return Base::equals(rhs); }
2101 /// @brief Component-wise inequality.
2102 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const Vec4& rhs) const noexcept { return !Base::equals(rhs); }
2103
2104 // ---- component-wise min/max ----
2105 /// @brief Take the component-wise minimum of @c *this and @a other in place.
2106 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4& minComponent(const Vec4& other) noexcept { Base::mergeMin(other); return *this; }
2107 /// @brief Take the component-wise maximum of @c *this and @a other in place.
2108 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4& maxComponent(const Vec4& other) noexcept { Base::mergeMax(other); return *this; }
2109
2110 /// @brief Return the smallest vector component
2111 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr ValueType min() const noexcept { return Base::smallestComponent(); }
2112 /// @brief Return the largest vector component
2113 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr ValueType max() const noexcept { return Base::largestComponent(); }
2114
2115 /// @brief Round each component down (toward negative infinity)
2116 /// @return Vec4<int32_t> (NanoVDB has no Coord4)
2117 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (floorAs uses non-constexpr math::Floor for floating point).
2118 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4<int32_t> floor() const noexcept { return Base::template floorAs<Vec4<int32_t>>(); }
2119 /// @brief Round each component up (toward positive infinity)
2120 /// @return Vec4<int32_t>
2121 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (ceilAs uses non-constexpr math::Ceil for floating point).
2122 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4<int32_t> ceil() const noexcept { return Base::template ceilAs<Vec4<int32_t>>(); }
2123 /// @brief Round each component to its closest integer value
2124 /// @return Vec4<int32_t>
2125 /// @note Only constexpr for integer @c T (roundAs uses non-constexpr math::Round for floating point).
2126 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Vec4<int32_t> round() const noexcept { return Base::template roundAs<Vec4<int32_t>>(); }
2127
2128 // ---- scalar * Vec / scalar / Vec (hidden friends — found only via ADL on Vec4,
2129 // never participate in unrelated namespace-scope overload sets) ----
2130
2131 /// @brief Scalar-on-the-left multiplication (hidden friend).
2132 template<typename T1>
2133 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr Vec4 operator*(T1 scalar, const Vec4& vec) noexcept
2134 {
2135 return Vec4(scalar * vec[0], scalar * vec[1], scalar * vec[2], scalar * vec[3]);
2136 }
2137 /// @brief Scalar-on-the-left division (hidden friend).
2138 template<typename T1>
2139 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] friend constexpr Vec4 operator/(T1 scalar, const Vec4& vec) noexcept
2140 {
2141 return Vec4(scalar / vec[0], scalar / vec[1], scalar / vec[2], scalar / vec[3]);
2142 }
2143}; // Vec4<T>

2145// ----------------------------> Vec2Aligned / Vec3Aligned / Vec4Aligned <------------
2146
2147/// @brief Opt-in over-aligned vectors for user-owned arrays, so each element can load
2148/// with one full-width vector instruction (e.g. 128 bits for @c Vec4Aligned<float>).
2149/// Whether that is faster depends on the access pattern and the GPU, so measure.
2150/// @details Each derives from its Vec class and converts to and from it, so the Vec
2151/// operators work unchanged and return the plain Vec type. @c Vec3Aligned is padded
2152/// to four components, so an array of them is not layout-compatible with an array of
2153/// @c Vec3. The plain Vec classes stay naturally aligned; see @c Vec4.
2154template<typename T>
2155struct alignas(2 * sizeof(T)) Vec2Aligned : Vec2<T>
2156{
2157 using Vec2<T>::Vec2;
2158 Vec2Aligned() noexcept = default;
2159 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec2Aligned(const Vec2<T>& v) noexcept : Vec2<T>(v) {}
2160};
2161
2162/// @brief Padded, over-aligned @c Vec3 for user-owned arrays; see @c Vec2Aligned.
2163template<typename T>
2164struct alignas(4 * sizeof(T)) Vec3Aligned : Vec3<T>
2165{
2166 using Vec3<T>::Vec3;
2167 Vec3Aligned() noexcept = default;
2168 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3Aligned(const Vec3<T>& v) noexcept : Vec3<T>(v) {}
2169};
2170
2171/// @brief Over-aligned @c Vec4 for user-owned arrays; see @c Vec2Aligned.
2172template<typename T>
2173struct alignas(4 * sizeof(T)) Vec4Aligned : Vec4<T>
2174{
2175 using Vec4<T>::Vec4;
2176 Vec4Aligned() noexcept = default;
2177 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec4Aligned(const Vec4<T>& v) noexcept : Vec4<T>(v) {}
2178};

2180// ----------------------------> matMult <--------------------------------------
2181//
2182// The matMult / matMultT overloads use plain arithmetic instead of fma / fmaf,
2183// which are not constexpr before C++23, so Map::applyMap and
2184// BBox<CoordT,false>::transform<Map> can be constexpr.
2185//
2186// The parentheses fix the accumulation order to right-to-left,
2187// x * m0 + (y * m1 + z * m2). With FP contraction and hardware FMA (nvcc's
2188// default -fmad=true, or GCC/Clang targeting an FMA-capable CPU) each step
2189// fuses into fma(x, m0, fma(y, m1, z * m2)). Without contraction each step
2190// rounds separately, and results may differ from the fused chain by ~1 ulp.
2191// Removing the parentheses reassociates the sum and loses the small terms
2192// under cancellation.
2193
2194/// @brief Multiply a 3x3 matrix and a 3d vector using 32bit floating point arithmetics
2195/// @note This corresponds to a linear mapping, e.g. scaling, rotation etc.
2196/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2197/// @param mat pointer to an array of floats with the 3x3 matrix
2198/// @param xyz input vector to be multiplied by the matrix
2199/// @return result of matrix-vector multiplication, i.e. mat x xyz
2200template<typename Vec3T>
2201__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMult(const float* mat, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2202{
2203 const float x = static_cast<float>(xyz[0]);
2204 const float y = static_cast<float>(xyz[1]);
2205 const float z = static_cast<float>(xyz[2]);
2206 return Vec3T(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[1] + z * mat[2]),
2207 x * mat[3] + (y * mat[4] + z * mat[5]),
2208 x * mat[6] + (y * mat[7] + z * mat[8]));
2209}
2210
2211/// @brief Multiply a 3x3 matrix and a 3d vector using 64bit floating point arithmetics
2212/// @note This corresponds to a linear mapping, e.g. scaling, rotation etc.
2213/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2214/// @param mat pointer to an array of floats with the 3x3 matrix
2215/// @param xyz input vector to be multiplied by the matrix
2216/// @return result of matrix-vector multiplication, i.e. mat x xyz
2217template<typename Vec3T>
2218__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMult(const double* mat, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2219{
2220 const double x = static_cast<double>(xyz[0]);
2221 const double y = static_cast<double>(xyz[1]);
2222 const double z = static_cast<double>(xyz[2]);
2223 using ValueT = std::decay_t<decltype(xyz[0])>;
2224 return Vec3T(ValueT(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[1] + z * mat[2])),
2225 ValueT(x * mat[3] + (y * mat[4] + z * mat[5])),
2226 ValueT(x * mat[6] + (y * mat[7] + z * mat[8])));
2227}
2228
2229/// @brief Multiply a 3x3 matrix to a 3d vector and add another 3d vector using 32bit floating point arithmetics
2230/// @note This corresponds to an affine transformation, i.e a linear mapping followed by a translation. e.g. scale/rotation and translation
2231/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2232/// @param mat pointer to an array of floats with the 3x3 matrix
2233/// @param vec 3d vector to be added AFTER the matrix multiplication
2234/// @param xyz input vector to be multiplied by the matrix and a translated by @c vec
2235/// @return result of affine transformation, i.e. (mat x xyz) + vec
2236template<typename Vec3T>
2237__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMult(const float* mat, const float* vec, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2238{
2239 const float x = static_cast<float>(xyz[0]);
2240 const float y = static_cast<float>(xyz[1]);
2241 const float z = static_cast<float>(xyz[2]);
2242 return Vec3T(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[1] + (z * mat[2] + vec[0])),
2243 x * mat[3] + (y * mat[4] + (z * mat[5] + vec[1])),
2244 x * mat[6] + (y * mat[7] + (z * mat[8] + vec[2])));
2245}
2246
2247/// @brief Multiply a 3x3 matrix to a 3d vector and add another 3d vector using 64bit floating point arithmetics
2248/// @note This corresponds to an affine transformation, i.e a linear mapping followed by a translation. e.g. scale/rotation and translation
2249/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2250/// @param mat pointer to an array of floats with the 3x3 matrix
2251/// @param vec 3d vector to be added AFTER the matrix multiplication
2252/// @param xyz input vector to be multiplied by the matrix and a translated by @c vec
2253/// @return result of affine transformation, i.e. (mat x xyz) + vec
2254template<typename Vec3T>
2255__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMult(const double* mat, const double* vec, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2256{
2257 const double x = static_cast<double>(xyz[0]);
2258 const double y = static_cast<double>(xyz[1]);
2259 const double z = static_cast<double>(xyz[2]);
2260 using ValueT = std::decay_t<decltype(xyz[0])>;
2261 return Vec3T(ValueT(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[1] + (z * mat[2] + vec[0]))),
2262 ValueT(x * mat[3] + (y * mat[4] + (z * mat[5] + vec[1]))),
2263 ValueT(x * mat[6] + (y * mat[7] + (z * mat[8] + vec[2]))));
2264}
2265
2266/// @brief Multiply the transposed of a 3x3 matrix and a 3d vector using 32bit floating point arithmetics
2267/// @note This corresponds to an inverse linear mapping, e.g. inverse scaling, inverse rotation etc.
2268/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2269/// @param mat pointer to an array of floats with the 3x3 matrix
2270/// @param xyz input vector to be multiplied by the transposed matrix
2271/// @return result of matrix-vector multiplication, i.e. mat^T x xyz
2272template<typename Vec3T>
2273__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMultT(const float* mat, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2274{
2275 const float x = static_cast<float>(xyz[0]);
2276 const float y = static_cast<float>(xyz[1]);
2277 const float z = static_cast<float>(xyz[2]);
2278 return Vec3T(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[3] + z * mat[6]),
2279 x * mat[1] + (y * mat[4] + z * mat[7]),
2280 x * mat[2] + (y * mat[5] + z * mat[8]));
2281}
2282
2283/// @brief Multiply the transposed of a 3x3 matrix and a 3d vector using 64bit floating point arithmetics
2284/// @note This corresponds to an inverse linear mapping, e.g. inverse scaling, inverse rotation etc.
2285/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2286/// @param mat pointer to an array of floats with the 3x3 matrix
2287/// @param xyz input vector to be multiplied by the transposed matrix
2288/// @return result of matrix-vector multiplication, i.e. mat^T x xyz
2289template<typename Vec3T>
2290__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMultT(const double* mat, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2291{
2292 const double x = static_cast<double>(xyz[0]);
2293 const double y = static_cast<double>(xyz[1]);
2294 const double z = static_cast<double>(xyz[2]);
2295 using ValueT = std::decay_t<decltype(xyz[0])>;
2296 return Vec3T(ValueT(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[3] + z * mat[6])),
2297 ValueT(x * mat[1] + (y * mat[4] + z * mat[7])),
2298 ValueT(x * mat[2] + (y * mat[5] + z * mat[8])));
2299}
2300
2301/// @brief Multiply the transpose of a 3x3 matrix by @a xyz and add @a vec (32-bit floats).
2302/// @note Corresponds to an inverse affine transform: @c (mat^T x xyz) + @c vec.
2303/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2304template<typename Vec3T>
2305__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMultT(const float* mat, const float* vec, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2306{
2307 const float x = static_cast<float>(xyz[0]);
2308 const float y = static_cast<float>(xyz[1]);
2309 const float z = static_cast<float>(xyz[2]);
2310 return Vec3T(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[3] + (z * mat[6] + vec[0])),
2311 x * mat[1] + (y * mat[4] + (z * mat[7] + vec[1])),
2312 x * mat[2] + (y * mat[5] + (z * mat[8] + vec[2])));
2313}
2314
2315/// @brief Multiply the transpose of a 3x3 matrix by @a xyz and add @a vec (64-bit floats).
2316/// @note Corresponds to an inverse affine transform: @c (mat^T x xyz) + @c vec.
2317/// @tparam Vec3T Template type of the input and output 3d vectors
2318template<typename Vec3T>
2319__hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] inline constexpr Vec3T matMultT(const double* mat, const double* vec, const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2320{
2321 const double x = static_cast<double>(xyz[0]);
2322 const double y = static_cast<double>(xyz[1]);
2323 const double z = static_cast<double>(xyz[2]);
2324 using ValueT = std::decay_t<decltype(xyz[0])>;
2325 return Vec3T(ValueT(x * mat[0] + (y * mat[3] + (z * mat[6] + vec[0]))),
2326 ValueT(x * mat[1] + (y * mat[4] + (z * mat[7] + vec[1]))),
2327 ValueT(x * mat[2] + (y * mat[5] + (z * mat[8] + vec[2]))));

2330// ----------------------------> BBox <-------------------------------------
2331
2332/// @brief Common base for floating-point and integer bounding boxes; not
2333/// constructible directly (only as a base of @c BBox).
2334/// @details Stores the closed-segment endpoints @c mCoord[0] (min corner) and
2335/// @c mCoord[1] (max corner). Whether the box is "min-inclusive max-inclusive"
2336/// or "min-inclusive max-exclusive" depends on the derived @c BBox
2337/// specialization (integer vs floating point).
2338template<typename Vec3T>
2339struct BaseBBox
2340{
2341 Vec3T mCoord[2];
2342 /// @brief Equality on the two corner points.
2343 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const BaseBBox& rhs) const noexcept { return mCoord[0] == rhs.mCoord[0] && mCoord[1] == rhs.mCoord[1]; };
2344 /// @brief Inequality on the two corner points.
2345 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const BaseBBox& rhs) const noexcept { return mCoord[0] != rhs.mCoord[0] || mCoord[1] != rhs.mCoord[1]; };
2346 /// @brief Indexed corner access: @a i = 0 returns min, @a i = 1 returns max.
2347 __hostdev__ constexpr const Vec3T& operator[](int i) const noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i >= 0 && i < 2); return mCoord[i]; }
2348 /// @brief Mutable variant of @c operator[].
2349 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3T& operator[](int i) noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(i >= 0 && i < 2); return mCoord[i]; }
2350 /// @brief Mutable accessor for the min corner.
2351 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3T& min() noexcept { return mCoord[0]; }
2352 /// @brief Mutable accessor for the max corner.
2353 __hostdev__ constexpr Vec3T& max() noexcept { return mCoord[1]; }
2354 /// @brief Const accessor for the min corner.
2355 __hostdev__ constexpr const Vec3T& min() const noexcept { return mCoord[0]; }
2356 /// @brief Const accessor for the max corner.
2357 __hostdev__ constexpr const Vec3T& max() const noexcept { return mCoord[1]; }
2358 /// @brief Translate (rigid-shift) both corners by @a xyz; return @c *this.
2359 __hostdev__ constexpr BaseBBox& translate(const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2360 {
2361 mCoord[0] += xyz;
2362 mCoord[1] += xyz;
2363 return *this;
2364 }
2365 /// @brief Expand this bounding box to enclose point @c xyz.
2366 __hostdev__ constexpr BaseBBox& expand(const Vec3T& xyz) noexcept
2367 {
2368 mCoord[0].minComponent(xyz);
2369 mCoord[1].maxComponent(xyz);
2370 return *this;
2371 }
2372
2373 /// @brief Expand this bounding box to enclose the given bounding box.
2374 __hostdev__ constexpr BaseBBox& expand(const BaseBBox& bbox) noexcept
2375 {
2376 mCoord[0].minComponent(bbox[0]);
2377 mCoord[1].maxComponent(bbox[1]);
2378 return *this;
2379 }
2380
2381 /// @brief Intersect this bounding box with the given bounding box.
2382 __hostdev__ constexpr BaseBBox& intersect(const BaseBBox& bbox) noexcept
2383 {
2384 mCoord[0].maxComponent(bbox[0]);
2385 mCoord[1].minComponent(bbox[1]);
2386 return *this;
2387 }
2388
2389 /// @brief Return @c true iff @a xyz lies in the closed box (each component
2390 /// satisfies @c min[i] <= @c xyz[i] <= @c max[i]).
2391 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool isInside(const Vec3T& xyz) const noexcept
2392 {
2393 if (xyz[0] < mCoord[0][0] || xyz[1] < mCoord[0][1] || xyz[2] < mCoord[0][2])
2394 return false;
2395 if (xyz[0] > mCoord[1][0] || xyz[1] > mCoord[1][1] || xyz[2] > mCoord[1][2])
2396 return false;
2397 return true;
2398 }
2399
2400protected:
2401 /// @brief Default-construct (leaves corners uninitialized — derived classes
2402 /// supply a meaningful default).
2403 __hostdev__ constexpr BaseBBox() noexcept {}
2404 /// @brief Construct from @a min and @a max corners directly.
2405 __hostdev__ constexpr BaseBBox(const Vec3T& min, const Vec3T& max) noexcept
2406 : mCoord{min, max}
2407 {
2408 }
2409}; // BaseBBox
2410
2411template<typename Vec3T, bool = util::is_floating_point<typename Vec3T::ValueType>::value>
2412struct BBox;
2413
2414/// @brief Partial template specialization for floating point coordinate types.
2415///
2416/// @note Min is inclusive and max is exclusive. If min = max the dimension of
2417/// the bounding box is zero and therefore it is also empty.
2418template<typename Vec3T>
2419struct BBox<Vec3T, true> : public BaseBBox<Vec3T>
2420{
2421 using Vec3Type = Vec3T;
2422 using ValueType = typename Vec3T::ValueType;
2423 static_assert(util::is_floating_point<ValueType>::value, "Expected a floating point coordinate type");
2424 using BaseT = BaseBBox<Vec3T>;
2425 using BaseT::mCoord;
2426 /// @brief Default construction sets BBox to an empty bbox
2427 __hostdev__ constexpr BBox() noexcept
2428 : BaseT(Vec3T( Maximum<typename Vec3T::ValueType>::value()),
2429 Vec3T(-Maximum<typename Vec3T::ValueType>::value()))
2430 {
2431 }
2432 /// @brief Construct from explicit @a min / @a max corners.
2433 __hostdev__ constexpr BBox(const Vec3T& min, const Vec3T& max) noexcept
2434 : BaseT(min, max)
2435 {
2436 }
2437 /// @brief Convert an integer @c Coord box into this floating-point box.
2438 /// @note @c max is exclusive in the floating-point convention, so the
2439 /// integer @c max corner is incremented by 1 before conversion.
2440 __hostdev__ constexpr BBox(const Coord& min, const Coord& max) noexcept
2441 : BaseT(Vec3T(ValueType(min[0]), ValueType(min[1]), ValueType(min[2])),
2442 Vec3T(ValueType(max[0] + 1), ValueType(max[1] + 1), ValueType(max[2] + 1)))
2443 {
2444 }
2445 /// @brief Return a cube-shaped @c BBox with min corner @a min and edge length @a dim.
2446 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr BBox createCube(const Coord& min, typename Coord::ValueType dim) noexcept
2447 {
2448 return BBox(min, min.offsetBy(dim));

2451 /// @brief Construct from a @c BaseBBox<Coord>; delegates to the @c (min, @c max) ctor.
2452 __hostdev__ constexpr BBox(const BaseBBox<Coord>& bbox) noexcept
2453 : BBox(bbox[0], bbox[1])
2454 {
2455 }
2456 /// @brief Return @c true if this bounding box is empty (max <= min in any axis).
2457 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool empty() const noexcept { return mCoord[0][0] >= mCoord[1][0] ||
2458 mCoord[0][1] >= mCoord[1][1] ||
2459 mCoord[0][2] >= mCoord[1][2]; }

2461 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr operator bool() const noexcept { return mCoord[0][0] < mCoord[1][0] &&
2462 mCoord[0][1] < mCoord[1][1] &&

2467 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool isInside(const Vec3T& p) const noexcept
2468 {
2469 return p[0] > mCoord[0][0] && p[1] > mCoord[0][1] && p[2] > mCoord[0][2] &&
2470 p[0] < mCoord[1][0] && p[1] < mCoord[1][1] && p[2] < mCoord[1][2];

2475/// @brief Partial template specialization for integer coordinate types
2476///
2477/// @note Both min and max are INCLUDED in the bbox so dim = max - min + 1. So,
2478/// if min = max the bounding box contains exactly one point and dim = 1!
2479template<typename CoordT>
2480struct BBox<CoordT, false> : public BaseBBox<CoordT>
2481{
2482 static_assert(util::is_same<int, typename CoordT::ValueType>::value, "Expected \"int\" coordinate type");
2483 using BaseT = BaseBBox<CoordT>;
2484 using BaseT::mCoord;
2485 /// @brief Iterator over the domain covered by a BBox
2486 /// @details z is the fastest-moving coordinate.
2487 class Iterator
2488 {
2489 const BBox& mBBox;
2490 CoordT mPos;
2491
2492 public:
2493 /// @brief Construct an iterator positioned at @c b.min().
2494 __hostdev__ constexpr Iterator(const BBox& b) noexcept
2495 : mBBox(b)
2496 , mPos(b.min())
2497 {
2498 }
2499 /// @brief Construct an iterator positioned at the given @a p inside @a b.
2500 __hostdev__ constexpr Iterator(const BBox& b, const Coord& p) noexcept
2501 : mBBox(b)
2502 , mPos(p)
2503 {
2504 }
2505 /// @brief Pre-increment: advance to the next coordinate in row-major z-fastest order.
2506 __hostdev__ constexpr Iterator& operator++() noexcept
2507 {
2508 if (mPos[2] < mBBox[1][2]) { // this is the most common case
2509 ++mPos[2];// increment z
2510 } else if (mPos[1] < mBBox[1][1]) {
2511 mPos[2] = mBBox[0][2];// reset z
2512 ++mPos[1];// increment y
2513 } else if (mPos[0] <= mBBox[1][0]) {
2514 mPos[2] = mBBox[0][2];// reset z
2515 mPos[1] = mBBox[0][1];// reset y
2516 ++mPos[0];// increment x
2517 }
2518 return *this;
2519 }
2520 /// @brief Post-increment: advance to the next coordinate; return a copy of the previous state.
2521 __hostdev__ constexpr Iterator operator++(int) noexcept
2522 {
2523 auto tmp = *this;
2524 ++(*this);
2525 return tmp;
2526 }
2527 /// @brief Iterator equality (asserts both iterators belong to the same @c BBox).
2528 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator==(const Iterator& rhs) const noexcept
2529 {
2530 NANOVDB_ASSERT(mBBox == rhs.mBBox);
2531 return mPos == rhs.mPos;
2532 }
2533 /// @brief Iterator inequality (asserts both iterators belong to the same @c BBox).
2534 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator!=(const Iterator& rhs) const noexcept
2535 {
2536 NANOVDB_ASSERT(mBBox == rhs.mBBox);
2537 return mPos != rhs.mPos;
2538 }
2539 /// @brief Lexicographic less-than over the underlying position.
2540 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator<(const Iterator& rhs) const noexcept
2541 {
2542 NANOVDB_ASSERT(mBBox == rhs.mBBox);
2543 return mPos < rhs.mPos;
2544 }
2545 /// @brief Lexicographic less-than-or-equal over the underlying position.
2546 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool operator<=(const Iterator& rhs) const noexcept
2547 {
2548 NANOVDB_ASSERT(mBBox == rhs.mBBox);
2549 return mPos <= rhs.mPos;
2550 }
2551 /// @brief Return @c true if the iterator still points to a valid coordinate.
2552 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr operator bool() const noexcept { return mPos <= mBBox[1]; }
2553 /// @brief Dereference to the current coordinate.
2554 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr const CoordT& operator*() const noexcept { return mPos; }
2555 }; // Iterator
2556 /// @brief Iterator positioned at the min corner.
2557 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Iterator begin() const noexcept { return Iterator{*this}; }
2558 /// @brief One-past-the-end iterator (max corner shifted by one in @c x).
2559 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr Iterator end() const noexcept { return Iterator{*this, CoordT(mCoord[1][0]+1, mCoord[0][1], mCoord[0][2])}; }
2560 /// @brief Default construct an empty bbox (@c min = @c CoordT::max(), @c max = @c CoordT::min()).
2561 __hostdev__ constexpr BBox() noexcept
2562 : BaseT(CoordT::max(), CoordT::min())
2563 {
2564 }
2565 /// @brief Construct from explicit @a min / @a max integer corners.
2566 __hostdev__ constexpr BBox(const CoordT& min, const CoordT& max) noexcept
2567 : BaseT(min, max)
2568 {
2569 }
2570
2571 /// @brief Splitting constructor (used by parallel range-based iteration).
2572 /// @details Halves the box along its longest axis: @c other keeps the upper
2573 /// half, the newly constructed @c BBox is the lower half. The @c SplitT tag
2574 /// type is ignored; it exists so this overload doesn't collide with the
2575 /// copy constructor.
2576 template<typename SplitT>
2577 __hostdev__ constexpr BBox(BBox& other, const SplitT&) noexcept
2578 : BaseT(other.mCoord[0], other.mCoord[1])
2579 {
2580 NANOVDB_ASSERT(this->is_divisible());
2581 const int n = MaxIndex(this->dim());
2582 mCoord[1][n] = (mCoord[0][n] + mCoord[1][n]) >> 1;
2583 other.mCoord[0][n] = mCoord[1][n] + 1;
2584 }
2585
2586 /// @brief Return a cube-shaped @c BBox with min corner @a min and edge length @a dim.
2587 /// @note Subtracts 1 from @a dim because the integer convention is min/max inclusive.
2588 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr BBox createCube(const CoordT& min, typename CoordT::ValueType dim) noexcept
2589 {
2590 return BBox(min, min.offsetBy(dim - 1));
2591 }
2592
2593 /// @brief Return a cube-shaped @c BBox spanning @a min..@a max in every axis.
2594 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] static constexpr BBox createCube(typename CoordT::ValueType min, typename CoordT::ValueType max) noexcept
2595 {
2596 return BBox(CoordT(min), CoordT(max));
2597 }
2598
2599 /// @brief Return @c true iff the box has more than one cell along every axis.
2600 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool is_divisible() const noexcept { return mCoord[0][0] < mCoord[1][0] &&
2601 mCoord[0][1] < mCoord[1][1] &&
2602 mCoord[0][2] < mCoord[1][2]; }
2603 /// @brief Return true if this bounding box is empty, e.g. uninitialized
2604 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool empty() const noexcept { return mCoord[0][0] > mCoord[1][0] ||
2605 mCoord[0][1] > mCoord[1][1] ||
2606 mCoord[0][2] > mCoord[1][2]; }
2607 /// @brief Convert this BBox to boolean true if it is not empty
2608 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr operator bool() const noexcept { return mCoord[0][0] <= mCoord[1][0] &&
2609 mCoord[0][1] <= mCoord[1][1] &&
2610 mCoord[0][2] <= mCoord[1][2]; }
2611 /// @brief Return the per-axis extent (max - min + 1 when non-empty, else 0).
2612 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr CoordT dim() const noexcept { return *this ? this->max() - this->min() + Coord(1) : Coord(0); }
2613 /// @brief Return the number of integer cells in the box, i.e. @c dim().x * @c dim().y * @c dim().z.
2614 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr uint64_t volume() const noexcept
2615 {
2616 auto d = this->dim();
2617 return uint64_t(d[0]) * uint64_t(d[1]) * uint64_t(d[2]);
2618 }
2619 /// @brief Return @c true iff the integer coordinate @a p lies inside the closed box.
2620 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool isInside(const CoordT& p) const noexcept { return !(CoordT::lessThan(p, this->min()) || CoordT::lessThan(this->max(), p)); }
2621 /// @brief Return @c true if the given bounding box is inside this bounding box.
2622 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool isInside(const BBox& b) const noexcept
2623 {
2624 return !(CoordT::lessThan(b.min(), this->min()) || CoordT::lessThan(this->max(), b.max()));
2625 }
2626
2627 /// @brief Return @c true if the given bounding box overlaps with this bounding box.
2628 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr bool hasOverlap(const BBox& b) const noexcept
2629 {
2630 return !(CoordT::lessThan(this->max(), b.min()) || CoordT::lessThan(b.max(), this->min()));
2631 }
2632
2633 /// @warning This converts a CoordBBox into a floating-point bounding box which implies that max += 1 !
2634 template<typename RealT = double>
2635 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr BBox<Vec3<RealT>> asReal() const noexcept
2636 {
2637 static_assert(util::is_floating_point<RealT>::value, "CoordBBox::asReal: Expected a floating point coordinate");
2638 return BBox<Vec3<RealT>>(Vec3<RealT>(RealT(mCoord[0][0]), RealT(mCoord[0][1]), RealT(mCoord[0][2])),
2639 Vec3<RealT>(RealT(mCoord[1][0] + 1), RealT(mCoord[1][1] + 1), RealT(mCoord[1][2] + 1)));
2640 }
2641 /// @brief Return a new instance that is expanded by the specified padding.
2642 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr BBox expandBy(typename CoordT::ValueType padding) const noexcept
2643 {
2644 return BBox(mCoord[0].offsetBy(-padding), mCoord[1].offsetBy(padding));
2645 }
2646
2647 /// @brief Transform this coordinate bounding box by the specified map.
2648 /// @param map mapping of index to world coordinates
2649 /// @return world bounding box
2650 template<typename Map>
2651 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr auto transform(const Map& map) const noexcept
2652 {
2653 using Vec3T = Vec3<double>;
2654 const Vec3T tmp = map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[0][0], mCoord[0][1], mCoord[0][2]));
2655 BBox<Vec3T> bbox(tmp, tmp);// return value
2656 bbox.expand(map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[0][0], mCoord[0][1], mCoord[1][2])));
2657 bbox.expand(map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[0][0], mCoord[1][1], mCoord[0][2])));
2658 bbox.expand(map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[1][0], mCoord[0][1], mCoord[0][2])));
2659 bbox.expand(map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[1][0], mCoord[1][1], mCoord[0][2])));
2660 bbox.expand(map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[1][0], mCoord[0][1], mCoord[1][2])));
2661 bbox.expand(map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[0][0], mCoord[1][1], mCoord[1][2])));
2662 bbox.expand(map.applyMap(Vec3T(mCoord[1][0], mCoord[1][1], mCoord[1][2])));
2663 return bbox;
2664 }
2665
2666#if defined(__CUDACC__) // the following functions only run on the GPU!
2667 /// @brief Device-only: atomically expand the box to enclose the integer point @a ijk.
2668 __device__ inline BBox& expandAtomic(const CoordT& ijk) noexcept
2669 {
2670 mCoord[0].minComponentAtomic(ijk);
2671 mCoord[1].maxComponentAtomic(ijk);
2672 return *this;
2673 }
2674 /// @brief Device-only: atomically expand the box to enclose another @a bbox.
2675 __device__ inline BBox& expandAtomic(const BBox& bbox) noexcept
2676 {
2677 mCoord[0].minComponentAtomic(bbox[0]);
2678 mCoord[1].maxComponentAtomic(bbox[1]);
2679 return *this;
2680 }
2681 /// @brief Device-only: atomically intersect this box with @a bbox.
2682 __device__ inline BBox& intersectAtomic(const BBox& bbox) noexcept
2683 {
2684 mCoord[0].maxComponentAtomic(bbox[0]);
2685 mCoord[1].minComponentAtomic(bbox[1]);
2686 return *this;
2687 }
2688#endif
2689}; // BBox<CoordT, false>

2693/// @brief 8-bit red, green, blue, alpha packed into 32 bit unsigned int
2694class Rgba8
2695{
2696 union
2697 {
2698 uint8_t c[4]; // 4 integer color channels of red, green, blue and alpha components.
2699 uint32_t packed; // 32 bit packed representation
2700 } mData;
2701
2702public:
2703 static const int SIZE = 4;
2704 using ValueType = uint8_t;
2705
2706 /// @brief Default copy constructor
2707 Rgba8(const Rgba8&) noexcept = default;
2708
2709 /// @brief Default move constructor
2710 Rgba8(Rgba8&&) noexcept = default;
2711
2712 /// @brief Default move assignment operator
2713 /// @return non-const reference to this instance
2714 Rgba8& operator=(Rgba8&&) noexcept = default;
2715
2716 /// @brief Default copy assignment operator
2717 /// @return non-const reference to this instance
2718 Rgba8& operator=(const Rgba8&) noexcept = default;
2719
2720 /// @brief Default ctor initializes all channels to zero
2721 __hostdev__ constexpr Rgba8() noexcept
2722 : mData{{0, 0, 0, 0}}
2723 {
2724 static_assert(sizeof(uint32_t) == sizeof(Rgba8), "Unexpected sizeof");
2725 }
2726
2727 /// @brief integer r,g,b,a ctor where alpha channel defaults to opaque
2728 /// @note all values should be in the range 0u to 255u
2729 __hostdev__ constexpr Rgba8(uint8_t r, uint8_t g, uint8_t b, uint8_t a = 255u) noexcept
2730 : mData{{r, g, b, a}}
2731 {
2732 }
2733
2734 /// @brief Ctor where all channels are initialized to the same value.
2735 /// @note value should be in the range 0u to 255u
2736 explicit __hostdev__ constexpr Rgba8(uint8_t v) noexcept
2737 : mData{{v, v, v, v}}
2738 {
2739 }
2740
2741 /// @brief floating-point r,g,b,a ctor where alpha channel defaults to opaque
2742 /// @note all values should be in the range 0.0f to 1.0f
2743 __hostdev__ constexpr Rgba8(float r, float g, float b, float a = 1.0f) noexcept
2744 : mData{{static_cast<uint8_t>(0.5f + r * 255.0f), // round floats to nearest integers
2745 static_cast<uint8_t>(0.5f + g * 255.0f), // double {{}} is needed due to union
2746 static_cast<uint8_t>(0.5f + b * 255.0f),
2747 static_cast<uint8_t>(0.5f + a * 255.0f)}}
2748 {
2749 }
2750
2751 /// @brief Construct from a @c Vec3<float> with rgb components (alpha set to opaque).
2752 /// @note all values should be in the range 0.0f to 1.0f
2753 __hostdev__ constexpr Rgba8(const Vec3<float>& rgb) noexcept
2754 : Rgba8(rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2])
2755 {
2756 }
2757
2758 /// @brief Construct from a @c Vec4<float> with rgba components.
2759 /// @note all values should be in the range 0.0f to 1.0f
2760 __hostdev__ constexpr Rgba8(const Vec4<float>& rgba) noexcept
2761 : Rgba8(rgba[0], rgba[1], rgba[2], rgba[3])
2762 {
2763 }
2764
2765 /// @brief Compare on the 32-bit packed integer representation (lexicographic by byte).
2766 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] bool operator< (const Rgba8& rhs) const noexcept { return mData.packed < rhs.mData.packed; }
2767 /// @brief Equality on the 32-bit packed integer representation.
2768 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] bool operator==(const Rgba8& rhs) const noexcept { return mData.packed == rhs.mData.packed; }
2769 /// @brief Return the squared L2 length of the rgb channels in the [0, 1] range
2770 /// (alpha is ignored). @c 0.0000153787005f is @c 1/255^2.
2771 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr float lengthSqr() const noexcept
2772 {
2773 return 0.0000153787005f * (float(mData.c[0]) * mData.c[0] +
2774 float(mData.c[1]) * mData.c[1] +
2775 float(mData.c[2]) * mData.c[2]); //1/255^2
2776 }
2777 /// @brief L2 length of the rgb channels (alpha ignored). Not @c constexpr — calls @c sqrtf.
2778 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] float length() const noexcept { return sqrtf(this->lengthSqr()); }
2779 /// @brief Return the @a n'th color channel as a float in the range 0 to 1.
2780 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr float asFloat(int n) const noexcept { return 0.003921569f*float(mData.c[n]); }// divide by 255
2781 /// @brief Indexed channel access. Asserts @c 0 <= @a n < 4 in debug builds.
2782 __hostdev__ constexpr const uint8_t& operator[](int n) const noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < 4); return mData.c[n]; }
2783 /// @brief Mutable variant of @c operator[].
2784 __hostdev__ constexpr uint8_t& operator[](int n) noexcept { NANOVDB_ASSERT(n >= 0 && n < 4); return mData.c[n]; }
2785 /// @brief Const access to the 32-bit packed integer representation.
2786 __hostdev__ const uint32_t& packed() const noexcept { return mData.packed; }
2787 /// @brief Mutable access to the 32-bit packed integer representation.
2788 __hostdev__ uint32_t& packed() noexcept { return mData.packed; }
2789 //@{
2790 /// @brief Named channel accessors (r, g, b, a). Both const and non-const variants.
2791 __hostdev__ constexpr const uint8_t& r() const noexcept { return mData.c[0]; }
2792 __hostdev__ constexpr const uint8_t& g() const noexcept { return mData.c[1]; }
2793 __hostdev__ constexpr const uint8_t& b() const noexcept { return mData.c[2]; }
2794 __hostdev__ constexpr const uint8_t& a() const noexcept { return mData.c[3]; }
2795 __hostdev__ constexpr uint8_t& r() noexcept { return mData.c[0]; }
2796 __hostdev__ constexpr uint8_t& g() noexcept { return mData.c[1]; }
2797 __hostdev__ constexpr uint8_t& b() noexcept { return mData.c[2]; }
2798 __hostdev__ constexpr uint8_t& a() noexcept { return mData.c[3]; }
2799 //@}
2800 /// @brief Implicit conversion to a @c Vec3<float> with channels in [0, 1] (alpha dropped).
2801 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr operator Vec3<float>() const noexcept {
2802 return Vec3<float>(this->asFloat(0), this->asFloat(1), this->asFloat(2));
2803 }
2804 /// @brief Implicit conversion to a @c Vec4<float> with rgba channels in [0, 1].
2805 __hostdev__ [[nodiscard]] constexpr operator Vec4<float>() const noexcept {
2806 return Vec4<float>(this->asFloat(0), this->asFloat(1), this->asFloat(2), this->asFloat(3));
2807 }
2808}; // Rgba8
